questions.stem: In which of the following types of angioedema is the C4 level usually within the normal range?
options: Acquired angioedema associated with B-cell lymphoma.
questions.explanation:
An easy way to remember this is that all types of angioedema, with the exception of hereditary angioedema type III, angioedema as part of urticaria, and ACE inhibitor angiooedema are usually associated with low levels of C4.
In hereditary angioedema type I, Cl esterase inhibitor levels are reduced, however in type II the Cl esterase inhibitor levels may be normal or elevated but the functional Cl inhibitor activity is decreased.
Type III hereditary angioedema is exceptionally rare and is associated with norm.:il levels of both C4 and Cl esterase inhibitor. It is caused by mutation in factor XII.
Type III hereditary angioedema is mostly seen in female patients and can be aggravated by oestrogens. Diagnosis is often difficult and requires identification of factor XII mutation.
Acquired angioedema can occur secondary to lymphoproliferative disorders, or systemic lupus erythematosus. This is associated with low leveis of both C4 and Cl esterase inhibitor levels and a positive anti-Clq antibody.
The presence of anti-Clq antibody will help differentiate acquired angioedema (secondary to lymphoproliferative disorders or systemic lupus erythematosus) frcm hereditary angioedema in new cases where there is no family history.

questions.stem: Which of the following is not a physical urticaria?
questions.explanation:
Other forms of physical urticarias include: cholinergic, vibratory, aquagenic and exercise-induced urticaria (exercise following the ingestion of shell fish and wheat are the commonest triggers).
Hereditary angioedema should be considered in isolated angioedema unresponsive to anti-histamines or corticosteroids.
Low complement 4 levels are always found during the attacks (except in type 3 hereditary angioedema).

questions.stem: Latex can cross-react with all of the following except:
questions.explanation:
Peanuts are legumes and can cross-react with beans, soya, peas and lentils.
Cross-reaction with "tree nuts" may also occur.
Cross-reaction of latex with certain fruits give rise to the "latex-fruit allergy syndrome" in which the symptoms are similar to the "oral allergy syndrome" that occurs due to the cross-reaction of birch pollen with certain fruits such as apples and pears.
The symptoms are mainly of contact urticaria (typP.-1 allergy).

questions.stem: A 65-year-old man presents with photo-distributed eczema that is worse each time he works in his garden. You therefore suspect allergic contact dermatitis and perform patch testing to series which include chemicals and plants. Which of the following chemicals is found predominantly in wood?
questions.explanation:
Dalberglones are chemicals found mainly in wood and should therefore be suspected in wood cutters.
Tulpulin-A is the main allergen found in Tulips.
Primin is the main allergen in the Primula plant.
Sesquiterpene lactone mix is an allergen found in many plants and therefore can serve in many cases as a "screening" for possible plant allergy.
Other chemicals that can be found in plants or trees include oak, moss, terpenes and propolis.

questions.stem: A 46-year-old woman has been complaining of intractable vulval dermatitis for the last five years for which she has tried several prescribed and over-the-counter preparations, some of which aggravates her dermatitis. You suspect allergic contact dermatitis and therefore advise patch testing. Which of the following allergens is least likely to be relevant in thiscase?
questions.explanation:
Nickel Sulphate is the most commonly found allergen including in patients who have been patched for vulval contact dermatitis however, it is the least likely to be relevant in this situation.
Vulval contact dermatitis is often caused by preservatives, topical anaesthetics, perfumes, neomycin and patients' own products.
More recently, in the United Kingdom, positive patch test reactions to sodium metablsulphite, as in trimovate cream, have been increasingly seen in this condition.

questions.stem: Peri-orbital oedema is most likely to occur in which of the following conditions?
questions.explanation: Other causes of peri-orbital oedema include allergic contact dermatitis to cosmetics or PPD with or without overt scalp dermatitis, dermatomyositis,angio-oedema, erysipelas, nephrotic syndrome and hypothyroidism.

questions.stem: Which of the following chemicals is not a preservative?
questions.explanation:
Mercaptobenzothiazole is a rubber allergen. It should therefore be suspected in cases where there is a suspicion of rubber allergy such as the use of glov s or in suspected shoe dematitis.
Other rubber allergens include carba and thiuram mix.
Other preservatives include the isothlozilinones, gluteraldehyde and all the formaldehyde releasers.

questions.stem: You patch test a 36-year-old lady who gave a history of worsening of her eczema with the use of certain topical preparations and you found a strong positive reaction to benzalkonium chloride. Which of the following topical preparations is safe to use?
questions.explanation:
Benzalkonium chloride is an anti-microbial chemical added in many preparations of emollients and antiseptics.
Oilatum plus contains benzalkonium chloride however, all other products of oilatum do not contain this chemical.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements regarding poison ivy is correct?
options: Poison ivy sensitive individuals can develop peri-oral dermatitis from eating bananas.
Rubber gloves are safe to use in sensitized individuals when in contact with the plant.
The allergen responsible following contact with the plant is urushiol.
The allergen responsible for the dermatitis following contact with the plant is primin.
The highest rate of sensitization is found in South East Asia.
questions.explanation:
Primin is the allergen found in the primula plant.
Peri-oral dermatitis to mangoes may occur in sensitized individuals.
Banana can cross react with latex.
The highest rate of sensitization to urushiol (responsible for poison ivy) is in North America.
Urushiol is soluble in rubber and therefore vinyl gloves should be worn for protection.

questions.stem: Which of the following tattoo pigments should be avoided in a patient with a known contact allergy tc cement?
questions.explanation:
Chromium and cobalt are both present in cement.
Red tattoos can contain mercury, ferric hydrate and/or oxide.
Manganese is an inorganir. salt often found in purple tattoos.

questions.stem: Which of the following delayed reactions to tattoos is the commonest?
questions.explanation:
Reactions to tattoos can either be acute or delayed.
The majority of allergic contact dermatitis is related to red tattoos.
Red tattoos are either due to inorganic salts of metals such as mercury or cinnabar; or due to organic preparations such as sandalwood and brazilwood.
Patch testing will only be positive to the inorganic salts (i.e. mercury) and not to the organic salts due to the water insolubility of the latter.
Mercury pigment is also responsible for the delayed lichenoid reactions to tattoos but patch testing will be negative and the clinical and histological appearances will differ from those of allergic contact dermatitis.
In pseudolymphomas the lymphocytes are polyclonal as opposed to monoclonal in cutaneous lymphomas.

questions.stem: A patient is said to have chronic urticaria if the urticaria symptoms occur for more than 6 weeks. In addition, which of the following criteria should be fulfilled for urticaria to be classified as 'chronic'?
options: Urticaria occurring at least once a week off treatment.
Urticaria occurring at least twice a week off treatment.
Urticaria occurring at least twice a week on treatment.
Urticaria occurring at least three times a week off treatment.
Urticaria occurring at least three times a week on treatment.
questions.explanation:
The term 'chronic urticaria' is applied to continuous urticaria occurring at least twice a week off treatment.
Urticaria occurring less frequently than this is called episodic (or recurrent).
Episodic urticaria is more likely to have an identifiable environmental trigger.

questions.stem: Physical urticarias are induced by an exogenous physical stimulus. Which of the following is the most common physical urticaria?
questions.explanation:
Immediate dermographism can be either simple or symptomatic.
Simple immediate dermographism occurs in about 5% of normal people.
It occurs in response to moderate stroking of the skin.
Symptomatic dermographism is the most common type of the physical urticarias.
It manifests as linear wheals at sites of scratching or friction.
Delayed dermographism often occurs after 30 mins of stroking the skin.
Delayed pressure urticaria is characterized by the development of deep erythematous swellings at sites of sustained pressure to the skin, 30 minutes to 12 hours later.
Cholinergic urticaria presents with multiple transient papular wheals 2-3 mm in diameter which occur within 15 minutes of physical exertion, hot baths, or emotional stress.
Exercise-induced anaphylaxis (EIA) and Food-and exercise-induced anaphylaxis (FEIA) are increasingly recognized syndromes.
In FEIA, angioedema and/or anaphylaxis occur within minutes of exercise if it follows either prior ingestion of a specific food (e.g. wheat), or sometimes within 4 hours of a heavy meal.
EIA is produced by exercise, but unlike cholinergic urticaria, not by an increase in core temperature induced by other means.

questions.stem: A 23-year man presents with severe facial dermatitis. The problem appeared during a recent camping holiday during which time he used safety matches on a daily basis. Type-4 hypersensitivity has likely developed to which of the following agents?
questions.explanation:
Phosphorus sesquisulfide is found in match tips and friction strips of safety match boxes.
The other agents listed are formaldehyde releasers.

questions.stem: Skin prick testing in a 21-year-old female nurse confirms the clinical suspicion of latex allergy. Which of the following factors carries the greatest risk of mortality during any future anaphylactic attack?
options: Strength of skin prick response to latex.
Family history of death during anaphylaxis.
questions.explanation:
Poorly controlled asthma is cited as the single most important risk factor for fatal anaphylaxis, especially in children and young adults, and can be an indication for self-in jectable adrenaline.
The life-saving intervention during anaphylaxis is adrenaline, delivered via the intramuscular route.
In adults the dose is 500 micrograms (0.S ml of 1:1000 adrenaline).

questions.stem: All of the following drugs can aggravate spontaneous urticaria except:
questions.explanation:
Several drugs may trigger or aggravate an attack of urticaria which include non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs, opiates and ACE-inhibitors.
Alcohol and stress can have a similar effect.
Montelukast is a leukotriene antagonist often used in addition to the anti-histamines in the treatment of urticaria.
ACE-inhibitors can also produce isolated angioedema in absence of any wheals due to the inhibition of the breakdown of bradykinin which is different from the urticarial
wheals triggered by ACE-inhibitors through histamine released from mast cells.

questions.stem: Which of the following food allergies are most likely to persist into adulthood when seen in childhood (particularly in the presence of atopic dermatitis)?
questions.explanation:
Food allergies are common in children with atopic background which in some children can worsen the eczema or be associated with episodes of urticaria on ingestion of the particular food item.
Allergies to peanuts, fish and shell fish are most likely to persist into adulthood.
Correct diagnosis of food allergy includes a detailed history complemented by skin prick testing and RAST testing in selected cases.

questions.stem: You patch test a 37-year-old woman due to worsening of her eczema despite the use of several topical treatments and found that she has a ++ reaction to chlorocresol. Which of the following treatments can she use safely?
questions.explanation:
Chlorocresol is a preservative found in many topical treatments including Eumovate, Betnovate an-:l Fucibet creams.
Dermovate cream does contain Chlorocresol but the ointment formula does not and is therefore safe to use in this particular case.
Hydrocortisone preparations do not contain Chlorocresol.

questions.stem: Which of the following conditions is an example of non-IgE-mediated reactions?
questions.explanation:
Eosinophilic oesophagitis is a recently recognised condition in which a large number of eosinophilsinfiltrate the oesophageal mucosa resulting in inflammation.
It has been increasingly found in patients with severe atopic disease and presents with dysphagia and reflux disease.
Colicky abdominal pain can be mediated through IgE to a food allergen in the absence of skin manifestations.
Oral allergy syndrome is a type of IgE-mediated reaction to certain food items, which often cross react with pollen allergy.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the safest method of administering a drug to avoid sensitization?
questions.explanation:
Oral administration of a drug is least likely to produce sensitization.
Intramuscular is the most likely parenteral way of eliciting drug sensitization.

questions.stem: A 26-year-old lady was referred for patch testing with persistent hand and facial eczema for the last year, which responds only partially to topical steroids and emollients. She had strong positive reactions to formaldehyde 1% on patch testing. Avoidance advice should be given for which of the following chemicals?
questions.explanation:
Patients who are allergic to formaldehyde should avoid the formaldehyde releas rs which include Quaternium 15, imidazolidinyl urea, DMDM Hydantoin and diazolidinyl urea.
Mercaptobenzothiazole is a rubber accelerator and reacts with carba mix and thiurams.

questions.stem: A 45-year-old woman presented with red, pruritic and swollen rash on the periorbital area, scalp and forehead. She had applied a hair dye 2 days before the onset of the rash. Patch testing demonstrates that she is allergic to para-phenyla'.Tline diamine (PPD). PPD can cross-react with the following:
questions.explanation: PPD cross-reacts with several other para-amine groups such as PADA, benzocaine and azo-dyes.

questions.stem: A 56-year-old man presented with bilateral eczema affecting the dorsal aspects o( his feet and has been present since he started wearing a pair of new shoes. It has been treated with topical steroids and ha was referred for patch testing. The most likely allergen in this case would be:
questions.explanation:
Potassium dichromate is often the c.ause of shoe allergy, as it is used for tanning of the leathers.
It can also be found in cement, and may often cross react with nickel sulphate and cobalt chloride.
Potassium dichromate can be an irritant, and if this is suspected, then testing to a lower concentration should be done.

questions.stem: A 35-year-old lady presented with three episodes of facial swelling, more noticeable in the peri-orbital area and swelling of both hands on one occasion. The swellings were more painful than pruritic, failed to respond to anti-histamines and a short course of oral corticosteroids. Her mother had similar episodes. Laboratory investigations revealed low C4 level, with normal Cl esterase inhibitor levels, but reduced functional Cl esterase levels. Her Clq antibodies were negative. The diagnosis here is:
questions.explanation:
The history and clinical findings are suggestive of the diagnosis of angio-oedema.
In the absence of urticaria and the lack of response to anti-histamines, one should suspect hereditary or acquired angio-oedema.
Hereditary angio-oedemas are autosomal dominant disorders.
The hallmark of both types 1 and 2 isreduced C4 level.
In hereditary angio-oedema type 1, both Cl inhibitor levels as well as Cl functional levels are reduced.
In hereditary angio-oedema type 2, Cl esterase inhibitor levels can be normal or elevated, but the functional levels are reduced.
Type 3 hereditary angio-oedema is very rare. C4 and Cl esterase inhibitor levels are normal. This condition tends to be precipitated by oestrogens.
A family history and absence of Clq antibodies go against the diagnosis of acquired angio-oedema.

questions.stem: A 46-year-old lady with a chronic eczematous rash on the hands and legs was referred for patch testing by a colleague as she gives a clear history of worsening of her "eczema" following the use of certain products. Patch testing showed a strong reaction to budesonide. Which other steroid preparation should be avoided by the patient?
questions.explanation:
Corticosteroids belong to 4 different chemical classes (A, B, C and D) which do not correspond to the potency.
Budesonide belongs to group Band therefore all corticosteroids from this group need to be avoided.
Group A consists of hydrocortisone acetate and tixocortolpivalate.
Group C consists of betamethasone and dexamethasone.
Group 01 consists of clobetasolpropionate and clobetasone butyrate.

questions.stem: A 23-year-old woman complains of an eczematous eruption on her face, which has been present for over a year and tends to worsen in the summer. She has noticed that the application of some sunscreens worsen her facial eczema. The most appropriate investigation would be:
questions.explanation:
The history and symptoms are suggestive of a photo-contact allergy In which the combination of a chemical (e.g. sunscreen) and ultraviolet light leads to an allergic contact dermatitis.
Although patch testing would be Indicated to exclude any contact allergy to the per fume, preservative or any chemical in the sunscreen, photo-patch testing is the investigation needed in suspected photo-contact allergy.
Skin prick and RAST testing are useful in detecting type-1allergy and are therefore not applicable in this setting.

questions.stem: A 23-year-old nurse was referred for patch testing as she has noticed the development of an eczematous eruption following the use of plasters or handling any adhesives. The most likely allergen in this case is:
questions.explanation:
Colophony is found in adhesives and plasters.
Primin is the chemical in the plant Primula obconica.
Propylene glycol is a preservative found in many products.
Benzocaine is found in topical anaesthetics and may cross-react with PPD, PABA and sulphonamides.

questions.stem: A colleague has performed a biopsy for a blistering condition and you receive the histology report stating that there is a subepidermal blister with a dense neutrophilic infiltrate; no eosinophils are seen. Direct immunofluoresence is not available. Which of the following disorders is most likely to show this histological appearance?
questions.explanation:
The type of cell infiltrate together with the direct immunofluoresence can be very helpful in establishing a histological differential.
Subepidermal bullae with a predominantly neutrophilic infiltrate include: linear IgA disease, dermatitis herpetiformis, mucous membrane pemphigoid, bullous lupus erythematosus and Sweet's syndrome.
Bullous mastocytosis has subepidermal bullae with mast cells.
Bullous pemphigoid has a predominantly eosinophilic infiltrate although a neutrophilic infiltrate may occur.
Erythema multiforme has a predominantly lymphocytic infiltrate.
Epidermolysis bullosa acquisita typically is cell-poor but some cases may have a neutrophilic infiltrate.

questions.stem: Which of the following alopecias has a predominantly neutrophilic infiltrate?
questions.explanation:
A predominantly neutrophilic infiltrate is found in folliculitis decalvans and dissecting cellulitis of the scalp.
A lymphocytic infiltrate is found in lichen planopilaris, alopecia mucinosa, cutaneous lupus erythematosus, alopecia areata and pseudopelade of Brocq, though In the iatter there may be little inflammation present.
Early acne necrotica and erosive pustular dermatosis can have a mixed neutrophilic and lymphocytic infiltrate.

questions.stem: Which of the following stain positively for cytokeratin?
questions.explanation:
Nodular amyloidosis is a rare primary cutaneous amyloidosis caused by the deposition of the AL amyloids produced by infiltrate of plasma cells. It is therefore often regarded as a plasmacytoma.
The other two types of cutaneous amyloidosis (macular and lichenoid) result from damaged keratinocytes; therefore they stain positively for cytokeratins.
Carcinoma en cuirasse is cutaneous metastasis from breast carcinoma, this like other epithelial tumours stain positively for cytokeratins.

questions.stem: In which of the following conditions is there typically no dyskeratosis at the suprabasal layer?
questions.explanation:
In Hailey-Hailey disease, there is acantholysis with usually little or no dyskeratosis.
Other acantholytic disorders in the absence of dyskeratosis include: pemphigus vulgaris, pemphigus vegetans and the acantholytic variant of actinic keratosis.
Conditions that can have both acontholysis and dyskeratosis include Darier's disease, Grover's disease, paraneoplastic pemphigus and warty dyskeratoma.
It is worth mentioning that in Hailey-Hailey disease, direct immunofluorescence is negative, which differentiates this condition from pemphigus vulgaris.

questions.stem: Mucin deposition is seen in which of the following cutaneous conditions?
questions.explanation:
Other conditions in which mucin deposition is found include reticular erythematous mucinosis, lichen myxoedema, sclerodermoid GVHD, granuloma annulare, and lupus erythematosus.
Myxoid cyst is the commonest mucin deposition condition.

questions.stem: Which of the following best represent corps ronds in Darier's disease?
questions.explanation:
Histological features of Darier's disease include:
Hyperkeratosis.
Focal dyskeratosis (premature, abnormal keratinisation of keratinocytes).
Eosinophilic dyskeratotic cells - corps ronds in the stratum spinosum, grains in the upper layers of the epidermis.
Corps ronds and grains correspond to apoptotic keratinocytes.
Suprabasal acantholysis and clefts.
Electron microscopy shows separation of the keratin filaments from the desmosomes and clumping of perinucleartonofilaments.

questions.stem: CD56 is a marker for which of the following cells?
questions.explanation:
CD56 is a helpful marker in the diagnosis of natural killer cells.
5100 and Melan-A are markers for melanocytes.
CD68 is a marker for macrophages.
CD20 and CD79a are markers for B-cells.
CO2, CD3, CD4, CDS, CD7 and CD8 are all markers ofT-cells.

questions.stem: A 60-year-old man presented with a relatively rapid onset of an erythematous-to-orange coloured eruption, which started initially on his face. It spread distally to involve most of his skin with some islands of normal skin on his trunk and limbs. Hi palms and soles have a shiny orange hue and subungual hyperkeratosis was noted. There is no personal or family history of psoriasis nor is there any joint involvement. What is the likely histological picture?
options: Dense infiltrate of plasma cells extending deep into the reticular dermis.
Parakeratosis alternating with orthokeratosis in both the horizontal and vertical plains.
Wedge-shaped hypergranulosis and the presence of dyskeratotic cells.
questions.explanation:
The clinical history here is of pityriasis rubra pilaris.
Histologically, this is characterised by alternating parakeratosis in the vertical and horizontal plains.
The main differential is psoriasis although the presence of islands of normal skin and the orange discolouration of the palms and soles favour the diagnosis of pityriasis rubra pilaris.

questions.stem: Parakeratosis is not a feature of which of the following?
questions.explanation:
Classic lichen planus is characterised by its absence of parakeratosis and eosinophils.
Parakeratosis can be found in all of the other listeci conditions.
Eosinophils in the context of a lichenoid infiltrate should raise the suspicion of a drug aetiology.

questions.stem: Sarcoidal granulomas can be seen in all of the following except?
questions.explanation:
Sarcoidal granulomas are so-called "naked" granulomas, which are characterised by the absence of necrosis.
Sarcoidal granulomas can be seen in Melkerson-Rosenthal syndrome and foreign body reaction to silica, beryllium and tattoo granulomas.
Granuloma annulare is characterised histologically by necrobiotic granulomas, which may also be seen in necrobiosis lipoidica, rheumatoid nodule and necrobiotic xanthogranuloma.

questions.stem: When differentiating between granuloma annulare and necrobiosis lipoidica histologically, which of the following statements is correct?
options: Abundant plasma cells may be seen in granuloma annulare.
Abundant plasma cells may be seen in necrobiosis lipoidica.
Necrobiosis lipoidica often has increased mucin deposition in the dermis.
Subcutaneousinvolvement is only a feature found in granuloma annulare.
The type of granuloma in granuloma annulare is sarcoidal.
questions.explanation:
Necrobiosis lipoidica can be differentiated from granuloma annulare by the abundance of plasma cells, sclerosis and the absence of mucin.
Whilst some cases of granuloma annulare can extend deep into the subcutis it is typically more superficilal than necrobiosis lipoidica and subcutaneous involvement is generally not a feature.
Both granuloma annulare and necrobiosis lipoidica are "necrobiotic" granulomas.

questions.stem: Spongiosis is least likely to be present in:
questions.explanation:
Although mild spongiosis can sometimes be found in cutaneous T celllymphoma, this is absent In cutaneous B cell lymphomas.
Other causes of spongiosis include pigmented purpuric dermatosis, erythroderma, Zoon's balanitis, insect bites and the pre-bullous stage of immunobullous disorders.

questions.stem: CD30 positivity can be seen in all of the following except:
questions.explanation:
Other causes of CD30 positivity include chronic tick bites and Sezary syndrome.
In marginal zone B cell lymphoma the infiltrate is positive for CD20, CD79a and bcl-2; and is negative for bcl-6 (positive in follicle centre B cell lymphoma).

questions.stem: Perineural invasion is typically not observed In which of the following:
questions.explanation:
Perineural invasion portends a poorer prognosis with increased risk for recurrence and metastasis.
Desmoplastic trichoepithelioma is a rare follicular tumour that histologically is in the differential of microcysticadnexal carcinoma and morphoeic basal cell carcinoma but typically, perineural Invasion is not seen.

questions.stem: You diagnose a patient as having pemphigus foliaceous and send the histology specimen to the pathologist. If your clinical diagnosis is correct, he should identify the split at:
questions.explanation:
Most patients with pemphigus vulgaris have mucosal membrane erosions.
The blisters of pemphigus vulgaris develop in the deeper portion of the epidermis, just above the basal cell layer.
Patients with pemphlgus foliaceus have only cutaneous involvement without mucosal lesions, and the splits occur in the superficial part of the epidermis, mostly at the granular layer.
154

questions.stem: In which of the following conditions can you see acantholysis in a skin biopsy?
questions.explanation:
Grover's disease characteristicallyshows acantholysis(separation and rounding off of keratinocytes) with or without dyskeratosis (abnormal keratinisatlon).
Bullous Pemphigoid is a sub-epidermal disorder with eosinophils.
Dermatitis herpetiformis is a chronic blistering condition with a sub-epidermal split and neutrophilic microabscesses.
Erythema multiforme and lupus erythematosus show an interface (lichenoid) reaction pattern.

questions.stem: Which of the following cysts lacks a granular cell layer?
questions.explanation: A pilar/ trichilemmal cyst lacks a granular cell layer and shows trichilemmal keratinlsation. The cyst is filled with homogenous, eosinophilic keratin unlike the laminated keratin found in an epidermoid cyst.

questions.stem: Microabscesses are seen in which of the following conditions?
questions.explanation:
Dermatitis herpetiformis shows papillary neutrophilic microabscesses.
Psoriasis can show Munro's microabscesses; these are collections of polymorphonuclear inflammatory cell infiltrate in the stratum cornem/ granular cell layer
Pautrier's microabscesses are a localised epidermal collections of atypical lymphoid cells as seen in T-cell lymphoma and mycosis fungoides.

questions.stem: Which of the following antibodies is used to highlight pagetoid spread in superficial spreading malignant melanoma?
questions.explanation:
CD31is a vascular marker.
CD30 is a marker for lymphomatoid papulosis and anaplastic large cell lymphoma.
MNF116 is a broad spectrum cytokeratin.
Alpha SMA (Smooth Muscle Actin) is a marker of smooth muscle tumours and myoepithelial tumours.

questions.stem: A 50-year-old male presents with a papular skin rash. Histological examination reveals granulomatous inflammation in the dermis. Which of the following markers or special stains will help in the diagnosis:
questions.explanation:
If there is granulmatous inflammation on skinbiopsy an infection should be excluded by performing special stains.
Mycobacterium tuberculosis can be visualised using the Ziehl-Neetsen stain.
PAS-Alcian blue is a pan-mucin combination.
Ber-EP4 and Melan-A are immunohistochemical antibodies.
Verhoeff-Van Gieson Stain is an elastic stain.

questions.stem: Select the marker most useful in differentiating basal cell carcinoma from basaloid squamous cell carcinoma:
questions.explanation:
Ber-EP4 is positive In basal cell carcinoma and negative in squamous cell carcinoma.
Epithelial membrane antigen (EMA) is positive in squamous cellcaniinoma and negative in basal cell carcinoma.
CEA is a marker of ductal differentiation.
Sl00 protein, HMB-45 and Melan-A are metanocytic markers.

questions.stem: A 45-year-old female presented with an itchy erythematous rash. Histological examination revealed a spongiotic dermatitis with neutrophils in the superficial keratin layer. Which of the following markers or special stains will help in the diagnosis:
questions.explanation:
If you see neutrophil polymorphs in the stratum corneum always rule out a dermatophyte infection by performing a PASO(Periodic acid-Schiff stain) with diastase. Diastase removes glycogen in keratinocytes making the fungi easier to see.
With PASD the,ell walls of fungi stain magenta.
Alternative fungal stain is Grocott's methenamine silver.

questions.stem: A 25-year-old female presents clinically with a changing mole. Skin biopsy reveals a lympho-histiocytic infiltrate with residual bland melanocytes. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation:
A halo naevus on biopsy shows a dense lymphocytic Infiltrate at the dermo-epider mal junction which often obscures the melanocytic component.
Reed's naevus is a variant of a Spitz's naevus.

questions.stem: A 44-year-old female presents with papules showing interface change and Civatte bodies on skin biopsy. What is your preferred diagnosis?
questions.explanation: Lichen planus has a band of chronic inflammatory cells at the dermo-epidermal junction with numerous Civatte bodies.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements about psoriasis is false:
options: Histologically shows spongiform pustule of Kogoj.
Shows interface change on skin biopsy.
Vascular ectasia is seen with margination of neutrophils.
questions.explanation:
Interface change/ lichenoid reaction pattern is not seen in psoriasis.
A biopsy showingaombined reaction pattern such as Interface change with psoriasiform hyperplasia or psoriasiform hyperplasia with spongiosis etc. one should consider a drug reaction.

questions.stem: In which of the following is Miescher radial granuloma a histopathological feature?
questions.explanation:
Miescher radial granuloma is composed of small, round, well-defined nodular aggregations of small histiocytes which are radially arranged around a minute silt.
It is a characteristic hlstopathologic marker of erythema nodosum.

questions.stem: A 26-year-old man of Jewish origin developed multiple shallow painful erosions In his mouth, multiple erosions on his trunk and limbs that start as flaccid bullae. Multiple swabs taken from the bullae and erosions showed commensals only. He has been referred for a diagno:.1ic biopsy, including immunofluorescence. Histologic.:al appearance of the biopsy would be:
options: Acanthosis and spongiosis throughout the epidermis.
questions.explanation:
The diagnosis is pemphigus vulgaris and therefore when blistering diseases are suspected, immunofluorescence samples should be taken.
In the case of pemphigus vulgaris, classic histological appearance would be of acantholysis and intra-epidermal blistering with positive immunofluorescence within the epidermis.
In pemphigus foliaceus, the split would be in the subcorneal layer with mucosal in volvement being typically absent.
The desmoglein is of type 1 in pemphlgus foliaceus and ispredominantly of type 3 in pemphigus vulgaris; however, desmoglein 1 can also be involved.

questions.stem: Which of the following is not an intra-epidermal blistering process?
questions.explanation:
The split in bullous amyloidosis is subepidermal. The blistering in other listed disorders is intra-epidemal.
In coma, the blistering may be subepidermal.
The thick corneal layers of the palms and soles are responsible for the "intact" blisters in the epidermis.

questions.stem: The blistering process in which of the following disorders is not subcorneal?
questions.explanation:
Toxic epidermal necrolysis results in full thickness epidermal necrosis.
Other conditions which result in subcorneal blistering include impetigo, subcorneal pustular dermatosis, infantile acropustulosis, erythema toxicumneonatorum, acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis and miliaria crystallina.

questions.stem: Which of the following conditions is not a true granulomatous disorder?
questions.explanation:
Granuloma faciale typically shows a vasculitic histology with no granulomas and the term "granuloma" here is therefore misleading.
A high-index of suspicion may be required to diagnose:1sh tank granuloma and if suspected, skin biopsy should be sent for mycobacterial cultures which can take several weeks.

questions.stem: You examine a lesion with a dermatoscope and find several maple leaf-like areas and arborising vessels. Which of the following do the above features best describe?
questions.explanation:
Other desmoplastic features of basal cell carcinoma (BCC) include blue-gray blotches, ovoid nests and globules in pigmented BCC, pink white shiny areas and spoke wheels.
131

questions.stem: Blue-grey ovoid nests and spoke wheeled pigmentation are evident on dermoscopic examination of a lesion. To which of the following do these features most likely relate?
questions.explanation: Other dermoscopic features of pigmented basal cell carcinomas, relating to melanin inclusion, may include: Absence of a true pigment network, blue-grey dots and globules, homogenous pigmented areas, peripheral leaf-like structures and specks of brown and grey pigment.

questions.stem: Which of the following would you not expect to see on dermatoscopic examination of a seborrhoeic keratosis?
questions.explanation:
Other dermoscopic features of seborrhoeic keratoses include: Comedo-like openings, homogenous pigmentation and milia-like cysts.
Presence of a pigment network is an atypical feature and raises the suspicion of a seborrhoeic keratosis-like (or verrucous) malignant melanoma.

questions.stem: A 65-year-old lady attends your clinic for review of an itchy erythematous plaque over her right upper chest. Examination under dermoscopy reveals a scattered grey granular pattern. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation:
Lichenoid keratosis is a benign lesion that is thought to develop from such lesions as a regressing solar lentigo or seborrhoeic keratosis.
They typically occur as a solitary lesion on the upper trunk and can resemble superficial basal cell crtrcinoma, Bowen's disease or even malignant melanoma.
The presence of a grey granular pattern under dermoscopy is a clue to diagnosisut alone is not enough to exclude more serious differentials.
Histological features include acanthosis and a band-like lichenoid lymphocytic infiltrate.
Parakeratosis may also be seen,serving as a distinguishingfeature from lichen planus.

questions.stem: A 1.9-year-old patient is referred for review of a lesion overlying her posterior shoulder. Her attention was first drawn to this when planning a tattoo of two intertwined serpents at the site. Examination under dermoscopy reveals streaks of pigmentation forming a peripheral starburst pattern. What is the most probable diagnosis?
questions.explanation:
Spitz or Reed naevi are relatively uncommon, mostly appear during childhood or early adult life.
They may be pigmented or non-pigmented.
The pigmented variety demonstrates a classic starburst pattern.

questions.stem: Which of the following vascular patterns would you expect on dermoscopic examination of a dear cell acanthoma?
options: Dot vessels lined up in a string of pearls.
questions.explanation:
Clear cell acanthoma (or Degas acanthoma) is a benign epithelial skin tumour.
Typical presentation is with a solitary shiny pink nodule, with wafer-like scaling around its edge.
Most common sites are the lower legs.
Histology demonstrates epidermal accumulation of clear glycogen-containing cells.

questions.stem: A 60-year-old man, with skin phenotype 3, is referred for urgent review of a solitary plaque on his left shin which he first noticed after a weekend gardening. Dermoscopy shows a central thrombosedlacune. Surrounding this are multiple smaller thrombosed and purple lacunes, over which there is a blue-white veil. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation:
Sporadic angiokeratoma typically present as solitary dark red to purple plaques, often with a scaly surface
They are composed of dilated capillaries and are often only come to medical attention after trauma leads to bleeding, thrombosis and sudden darkening.

questions.stem: A 30-year-old, 24-weeks pregnant patient has severe atopic eczema not responding to topical emollients alone. Which of the following drugs is an absolute contra-indication in pregnancy?
questions.explanation: Although generally systemic treatments should be avoided in pregnancy if possible, all the above, with the exception of mycophenolate mofetil, can be used in pregnancy.

questions.stem: Rifampicin may be an effective treatment for which of the following types of pruritus:
questions.explanation:
Rifampicin is an inducer of hepatic enzymes and can be effective in the treatmer.t of cholestatic pruritus.
Other treatments include cholestyramine and opioid receptor antagonists such as naltrexone.
UVB phototherapy, naltrexone and gabapentin can be used in uraemic pruritus.

questions.stem: A patient with severe psoriasis who is currently well-controlled on the anti- TNF biologic Etanercept (Enbrel) is planning to travel abroad and has asked your advice with regards to immunisations. Which vaccine is safe in this context?
questions.explanation:
Knowledge about vaccines in immunosuppressed patients is important as more pa tients are receiving anti-TNF therapy in dermatology.
Live vaccines must be avoided in patients who are receiving therapy with anti-TNF and these include: measles, mumps, rubella, small pox, yellow fever, dengue fever, BCG, polio, rabies, typhoid and varicella.
Pneumococcal vaccine can be used safely in this patient.

questions.stem: The mortality related to methotrexate has been primarily attributed to:
questions.explanation:
Idiosyncratic reactions can occur with any dose and are therefore dose-independent.
Oral ulcers may indicate methotrexate toxicity or folate deficiency.
Methotrexate should be used with caution in renal impairment.

questions.stem: A 58-year-old man complains of blurring of vision. He has been using a medication for hyperhidrosis. Which of the following is the most likely cause of his symptoms?
questions.explanation:
Glycopyrrolate is an anticholinergic agent which can be used in the treatment of compensatory, craniofacial, and diabetic gustatory hyperhidrosis.
It acts by preventing the acetylcholine-induced stimulation of the sweat gland receptors.
Its inability to cross the blood brain barrier, results in fewer side effects.
Systemically administered anticholinergic agents may result in dry mouth, visual disturbances, urinary retention and urgency, flushing and constipation.

questions.stem: A 56-year-old patient is commenced on ciclosporin for psoriasis. Which of the following is true regarding monitoring of ciclosporin therapy?
options: Ciclosporin dose should be reduced if serum creatinine increases by 30% above the baseline value.
Cliclosporinbloavailablllty remains uniform irrespective of the brand used.
GFR measurement should be carried out every 6 months for patients on long term ciclosporin.
Intake of grapefruit Juice should be encouraged.
Rise in blood pressure always necessitates additional drug therapy.
questions.explanation:
Ciclosporin dose should be reduced if serum creatinine increases by 30% above the baseline value (even if this increase is within the laboratory normal range).
Grapefruit juice interferes with gut cytochrome P-450 enzymes, which are important in metabolizing ciclosporin and therefore it should not beadministered simultaneously with ciclosporin.
Only a minority of patients (5-12%) develop new-onset hypertension during short course ciclosporin therapy, and the overwhelming majority of these cases respond to dose reduction and/or anti-hypertensive medication.
As ciclosporin nephropathy is closely related to duration of therapy, GFR should be assessed annually In patients receiving long-term continuous ciclosporin treatr:,ent.
Ciclosporin has formulation-dependent bioavailability with a wide inter-individual variability in absorption. Appropriate brand of ciclosporin should be consistently dispensed.

questions.stem: Which of the following drugs is implicated in the causation of ingrown toe nails?
questions.explanation: Ingrowing toenails can be caused by prescribed medications including retinoids, in dinavir and methotrexate.

questions.stem: In order to be "eligible" for funding to use biological therapy In severe chronic plaque psoriasis the patient must have tried and failed at least 2 systemic therapies and have:
options: DLQI and PASI both are equal to or more than 10.
DLQI and PASI both less than 10.
questions.explanation: The current guidelines state that in order to be eligible for biological therapy a patient must have severe disease and have a DLQI and a PASI equal to or greater than 10. Intolerance to or lack of response to systemic agents is?.n additional requirement. The NICE guidelines suggest that infliximab can be considered when the PASI is equal to or greater than 20 and the DLQI is over 18.

questions.stem: Which of the following biological therapies for psoriasis is administered intravenously?
questions.explanation:
infliximab is administered intravenously as a dose of 5 mg/kg at weeks 0, 2, 6 and every 8 weeks thereafter.
Dosing of ustekinumab is also weight-based: (i) 45 mg for patients under 100 kg, and, (ii)90 mg for those over 100 kg. It is administered subcutaneously.

questions.stem: With regards to anti-TNFtherapy in severe psoriasis in patients with congestive cardiac failure, the current British Association of Dermatologists recommendations are:
options: Avoidance in any New York Heart Association (NYHA) class.
Avoidance in NYHA class II and above.
Avoidance in NYHA class III and IV.
Safe to use with no risks in patients with cardiac failure.
questions.explanation:
Anti-TNF therapy should be avoided in patients with New York Heart Association (NYHA) class III and IV congestive cardiac failure.
Avoidance should also include patients with NYHA class I or II who have an ejection fraction of less than 50%.

questions.stem: Acitretin is a retinoid that can be used in psoriasis. Which of the following statements regarding this drug is true?
options: Combination with methotrexate increases the risk of hepatotoxicity.
Combination with tetracyclines increases the risk of benign intracranial hypertension.
Contraception should be continued for 2-3 years following discontinuation.
Hyperlipidaemia is one of the possible side-effects.
questions.explanation:
Acitretin can be used In psoriasis, Darier's disease, keratodermas, palmo-plantar pustulosis, hyperkeratotic hand eczema, and severe congenital ichthyoses.
The drug isvery teratogenic and should not be considered in women of child-bearing age. In extreme cases when it has to be used in this group, contraception must be ccntinued for at least 2-3 years following discontinuation of the drug.

questions.stem: Antibodies are most likely to be formed against which of the following drugs?
questions.explanation:
infliximab is a chimeric monoclonal antibody and therefore there is a high risk of developing antibodies against it in a proportion of patients. Reduced efficacy ran result due to the neutralising antibodies.
Antibodies can also be produced again-st adalimumab but to a lesser extent than infliximab.
Methotrex.ite can be combined with infliximab in cases where there is antibody production leading to loss of efficacy.

questions.stem: Based on available evidence, which of the following is considered the best option for treating morphea?
questions.explanation:
Methotrexate has the best evidence and should be the first-line treatment of choice in cases of generalized or accelerated morphea.
It can be combined with methyl prednisolone or preciinlsolone; the combmation has been shown to be very effective in cases of accelerated morphea.
Topical steroids, tacrolimus ointment or phototherapy can be used for localised morphea.

questions.stem: The combination of ciclosporin and statin therapy leads to increased levels oi statin which In turn can lead to statin-lnduced myopathy. Which of the following statins is however safe to combin with ciclosporin due to a different metabolic pathway?
questions.explanation:
This is an important reaction that dermatologists should be aware of as ciclosporin is metabolised through the CYP3A4 pathway.
Most statins, with the exception of pravastatin, are metabolised through the same metabolic pathway. Hence, this is the only statin that can be safely combined with ciclosporin.

questions.stem: Which of the following drugs is an absolute contra-indication in patients with active hepatitis B?
questions.explanation:
The use of immunosuppressive therapy should be avoided in patients with active hepatitis B and advice from the hepatologist should be sought.
Ciclosporin is an absolute contra-indication in active hepatitis B.
,.., Anti-TNF therapy can be used provided that adequate anti-viral therapy has been established.

questions.stem: A 45-year-old patient has severe pemphigus vulgaris. Which one of the drugs used to treat pemphigus has sterility as a side effect?
questions.explanation: Cyclophosphamide is given at a dose of 1-3 mg/kg/day (usually 50-200 mg/day) and its major side effects are haemorrhagic cystitis, sterility and leukopenia.

questions.stem: A 40-year-old man has been diagnosed with IgA pemphigus. Which of the following is the drug of choice in this condition?
questions.explanation:
,., Dapsone is the drug of choice in IgA pemphigus, although colchicine can be used in some c.ases.
,., A clinical response usually occurs within 24-48 hours.
,., Alternatively, sulphapyrldlne or acitretin can be used.
,., Low-to medium-dose prednisone, or photochemotherapy (PUVA) are other alternatives.

questions.stem: Which of the following medications is contraindicated in patients with known soya allergy?
questions.explanation: Allergy to soya is a contraindication to isotretinoin, as some brands of isotretinoin contain soya oil.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements regarding topical retinoidsis incorrect?
options: Their use is associated with increased resistance to the P.acnes bacteria.
They can exhibit an effect on micro-comedones.
Stimulation of collagen synthesis may occur.
questions.explanation:
Topical retinoids are widely used in the treatment of acne due to their effect on comedogenesis, increased collagen synthesis and reduction of post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation.
They can be used in the treatment of melasma due to down-regulation of the tyrosine synthesis which is essential for melanin production.
Its use does not lead to increased resistance to the P.acnes to antibiotics.
Unlicensed uses of topical retinoids include treating photo damaged skin.

questions.stem: Which of the following can be used as a depigmenting agent In the treatment o'f vitiligo?
questions.explanation:
Monobenzyl ether of hydroquinone (Monobenzone) is used for depigmentingresid· ual normal skin in patients with extensive vitiligo.
It is a phenolic toxin that destroys epidermal melanocytes.
it is available as a 20 percent cream.
Allergic and irritant reactions may occur.

questions.stem: In the United Kingdom, imiquimod cream (aldara) is not licensed for treatment of which of the following conditions?
questions.explanation:
imiquimod cream can be used for Bowen's disease; however this is an unlicensed treatment in this condition.
Its current licence is for genital warts, superficial basal cell carcinoma and actinic keratoses.

questions.stem: A 36-year-old man has been treated successfully with a systemic agent for his blistering disorder and reports a gradual weakness of his right foot, resulting in him trippingover several times. On examination, there was demonstrable motor weakness, with intact sensation. Which of the following drugs is most likely to be implicated in this case?
questions.explanation:
Dapsone is a11 antagonist of dihydropteroate synthetase and prevents the formation of folic acid.
It can be used in several blistering disorders, and motor-neuropathy is one of its possible long-term complications.
Hydroxychloroquine can cause retinopathy and this needs to be monitored for regularly.
Mepacrine is an anti-malarial drug, often used in conjunction with or as an alternative to hydroxychloroquine but does not cause ocular toxicity.

questions.stem: A 45-year-old man is admitted with severe desquamation of his skin following ingestion of phenytoin for epilepsy. Your consultant decides to start him on intravenous immunoglobulin. In the United Kingdom, intravenous immunoglobulins are licensed for use in which of the following conditions?
questions.explanation:
Intravenous immunoglobulins are used in several de;matological diseases, which include toxic epidermal necrolysis, pemphigus vulgaris, dermatomyositis and Kawasaki disease.
Currently, it only has a licence for use in Kawasaki disease among the dermatological conditions.

questions.stem: A 45-year-old patient is commenced on a new systemic medication. He returns 2 weeks later complaining of breathlessness and appears cyanosed. A blood film demonstrates methaemoglobulinaemia. Which of the following drugs used in certain dermatological conditions can cause methaemoglobulinaemia?
questions.explanation:
Oapsone can cause haemclysis and methaemoglobulinaemia.
Any patient who becomes breathless or cyanosed on dapsone must have his MetHb levels checked.
Methotrexate can cause pulmonary fibrosis (most commonly seen in patients with rheumatoid arthritis) and drug-induced pneumonitis, but can not cause methaemoglobulinaemia.
Fumaric acid esters can cause gastro-intestinal symptoms, flushing and a drop in the lymphocyte count.
Ciclosporin can cause hypertension and renal impairment and these should be regularly monitored.

questions.stem: Which of the following antibiotics in the treatment of acne is associated with the least resistance?
questions.explanation:
Antibiotic resistance is a growing problem in the treatment of acne.
It should be suspected in patients unresponsive to appropriate antibiotic therapy after 6 weeks of treatment.
Propionibacterium acne resistance has been documented with all macrolides and tetracyclines used in the treatment of acne.
Overall resistance is the highest with erythromycin and lowest with minocycline.
Measures to avoid antibiotic resistance should include avoidance of antibiotic monotherapy, limiting long-term use of antibiotics, and combining antibiotics with benzyl peroxide.
Recent studies do not show any benefit of using minocycline over other tetracyclines.

questions.stem: A 27-year-old woman with a long history of chronic plaque psoriasis has been suffering from an exacerbation of the disease with plaques covering approximately 40¼ of her body surface area. Her previous therapies included topical corticosteroids and phototherapy. She is due to get married in 2 months and is requesting a treatment that can rapidly help clear her psoriasis before her weddi1,g. She is otherwise well with r10 co-morbidities. The most appropriate systemic drug in the absence of any contra-indications would be:
questions.explanation:
Ciclosporin can induce rapid clearance as it acts quicker than most other systemic agents in psoriasis.
Main side-effects/complications that require regular monitoring are renal impairment and hypertension.
Prednisolone should not be used in psoriasis to avoid inducing pustular psoriasis following withdrawal.

questions.stem: Which of the following is not a recognized side-effect of the Epidermal Growth Factor Receptor (EGFR) antagonists?
questions.explanation:
The commonest side-effect of EGFRls is the papulo-pustular acneiform eruption; however comedones are typically absent.
Pyogenic granulomas and paronychiae are typically late-occurring side-effects (> 3 months).
Erythema nodosum can occur following certain drugs with oral contraceptives being the commonest.

questions.stem: A 45-year-old patient is commenced on methotrexat for his psoriasis. The action mode of methotrexate is by binding to:
questions.explanation:
Binding of methotrexate to dihdrofolate reductase results in the inhibition of the intracellular reduction of folate to tetrahydrofolate which in turn blocks the production of thymidine and purine biosynthesis.
The above process also leads to the inhibition of adhesion molecules and cytokines.
inosine monophosphate dehydrogenase is blocked by the drug mycophenolate mofetil which leads to the inhibition of the "de novo" biosynthesis of purines, leading to a reduction in DNA synthesis, nitric oxide production and adhesion molecules.

questions.stem: You refer a patient on long-term hydroxychloroquine to an ophthalmologist as he complains of some visual disturbances. Long-term, high doses of hydroxychloroquine can give rise to which ocular pathology?
questions.explanation:
The anti-malarial drug hydroxychloroquine is useful in cutaneous lupus.
Ocular toxicity can occur, particularly if doses exceed 6.5 mg/kg daily.
Regular ophthalmic examination which includes Amsler chart reading is mandatory.
Mepacrine, a drug often used in conjunction with or as a substitute of hydroxychloroquine does not cause ocular toxicity.

questions.stem: You plan to commence your patient on ciclosporin. The mode of action of ciclosporin is through binding to:
questions.explanation:
The binding-complex of ciclosporin and cyclophilin-A inhibits calcineurin which in turn inhibits the migration of transcription factor NFAT (nuclear factor of activated Tcells) into the cell nucleusresulting in the inhibition of IL-2.
inosine monophosphate dehydrogenase is Inhibited by mycophenolate mofetil.
Methotrexate binds to dihydrofolate reductase leading to the Inhibition of thymldine and purine biosynthesis.
CD20 is targeted by the relatively new monoclonal antibody drug rituximab which has been used in lupus and pemphigus.
Dihydropteroate synthetase is blocked by dapsone which prevents the formation of folic acid.

questions.stem: Which of the following pregnancy-related dermatoses is least likely to recur in subsequent pregnancies?
options: Pruritic urticarial papules and plaques of pregnancy (PUPP).
questions.explanation:
PUPP which is also called polymorphic eruption of pregnancy occurs in the first pregnancy and seldom recurs in subsequent pregnancies.
Both pemphigoid gestationis and intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy can recur with subsequent pregnancies or with the use of oral contraceptives.
Atopic eruption of pregnancy can be the first manifestation of atopic disease in a susceptible person.

questions.stem: A 24-year-old woman presents with excessive facial hair and acne. There is a history of menstrual irregularities as well. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation:
Hirsutism is defined as excessive terminal hair growth in women in the androge,1-sensitive areas.
Polycystic ovarian syndrome is the commonest endocrinological cause for:1irsutism.
Diagnosis of polycystic ovarian syndrome requires two out of three of the following:
positive imaging, menstrual abnormalities and signs of hyperandrogenism, which can be remembered by the acronym SAHA, that stands for Seborrohea, Acne, Hirsut,sm and Androgenetic alopecia.

questions.stem: Which of the following drugs is most likely to cause drug-induced linear IgA disease?
questions.explanation:
Vancomycin is the most common cause of drug induced linear IgA disease.
Penicillamine can cause both drug-induced pemphigus and mucous membrane pemphigoid, and long-term use can result in elastosis perforans serpiginosa, in which elastic fibres extrude through the epidermis.

questions.stem: Which of the following is not a feature of drug rash (or reaction) with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS) syndrome?
questions.explanation:
DRESS is a serious drugeruption that typically presents with an exanthematous eruption with fever, lymphadenopathy, oedema of the face, peripheral eosinophilia, atypical lymphocytes and visceral involvement.
Liver and kidney involvement may be seen.
The latency period may take anywhere between 1-8 weeks, although this may be much earlier with re-exposure to the drug.
A pustular eruption is not a feature of DRESS syndrome and is seen in acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis.

questions.stem: A 20-year-old man presents with acute onset of severe aciie associated with malaise, fever and arthralgia. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation:
Acne conglobata is a specific variant of acne characterised by large comedones with multiple openings, predominantly on the face and back.
A positive family history is often found and this should not be confused with acne fulminans which is a severe form of acne that tends to affect young males and presents with malaise, fever, arthralgia and liver involvement.
Unlike acne conglobata, haemorrhagic crusted ulcerative lesion can be found in acne fulminans.

questions.stem: Which of the following antibodies is most specific for systemic lupus erythematosus?
questions.explanation:
In systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) anti-nuclear antibody is positive in the majority of patients. Immunological abnormalities including the finding of anti-Sm and anti-dsDNA antibodies form one of the criteria for diagnosis of SLE.
Anti-Sm antibodies are specific to SLE and are found in around 20-30% of patients.
Anti-ds-DNA antibodies are also specific to this condition (also in "lupoid" hepatitis) and the titres may correlate with both renal involvement and disease activity (unlike the anti-Sm antibody).

questions.stem: Which of the following is associated with an abnormal lipid profile?
questions.explanation:
With the exception of xanthomata disseminatum, and verucciformxanthomas, all other types of xanthomas are associated with an abnormal lipid profile.
Eruptive xanthomata are often associated with elevated triglycerides as opposed to increased cholesterol levels in the other forms of xanthomata.
Xanthomata disseminatum is a histiocytic disorder.

questions.stem: A 40-year-old man presents with fever and red/purple tumid plaque 011the face for 3 days. A skin biopsy shows papillary dermal oedema and a dense, diffuse neutrophilic infiltrate in the reticular dermis. What is the most common malignancy associated with this presentation?
questions.explanation:
Ac1Jte febrile neutrophilic dermatosis (Sweet's syndrome), is a reactive process.
Abrupt onset of tender, red-to-purple papules coalesce to form plaques.
Commonest sites include upper extremities, face, or neck.
The rash is accompanied by fever and peripheral neutrophilia.
Causes include hematopoietic malignancies (most commonly acute myeloid leukemia), non-hematologic malignancies; e.g. genitourinary, breast, and gastrointestinal cancers, infectious most often involving the upper respiratory tract, drugs and systemic illnesses.

questions.stem: A 30-year-old woman developed erythematous patches and plaques on her trunk. These were associated with mild pruritus and progressed to become indurated and oedematous with few plaques developing blisters. She reported that previous patches and plaques resolved after several weeks leaving a green hue. She had no mucosal Involvement and laboratory investigations showed marked eosinophilia. A skin biopsy showed oedema, flame figures and an eosinophilic dermal infiltrate. Direct immunofluoresence was negative. The diagnosis is:
questions.explanation:
The history, clinical findings, histology and the presenci= of an eosinophilia fit with the diagnosis of eosinophilic cellulitis (Well's syndrome).
The condition can be associated with infections, ulcerative colitis, lymphoma and leukaemia.
Localized areas of eosinophilic cellulitis have been reported at injection sites of anti TNF drugs.
Topical or systemic corticosteroids are the treatment of choice.

questions.stem: Of which of the following conditions is livedo reticularis not a feature?
questions.explanation:
Kawasaki's disease is a medium-vessel vasculitis characterized by fever, conjunctival involvement, cervical lymphadenopathy, maculo-papular eruption on trunk and straw berry tongue.
Other causes of livedo reticularis include polyarteritis nodosa, phaeochromocytoma, multiple sclerosis and amantadine use.
A physiological variant exist-mainly following cold exposure -which disappears with re-warming.

questions.stem: Trachyonychia is a recognised feature of which of the following:
questions.explanation:
Trachyonychia - sand paper appearance and roughening of the nails.
Spontaneous resolution commonly occurs.
Other causes of trachonychia include: idiopathic, pemphigus vulgaris, psoriasis, li chen planus and eczema.

questions.stem: Which of the following does not portend a poor prognosis in alopecia areata?
questions.explanation:
Other poor prognostic factors include family history and chronicity.
Differential diagnoses include telogen effluvium, anagen effluvium, trichotillomania, loose anagen syndrome, drug-induced alopeda, systemic lupus erythematosus, syphilis and tinea capltis.

questions.stem: Which of the following is not a neutrophilic dermatosis:
questions.explanation:
Erythema multiforme is a reactive self-limiting condition which is predominantly lymphocytic.
Other examples of neutrophilic dermatoses include subcorneal pustular dermatosis and bowel-associateddermatosis-arthritis syndrome.
The neutrophilic derm;;toses can beassociated with internal disease/haematological malignancies and often respond well to systemic corticosteriods.

questions.stem: A 39-year-old man developed fever, neutrophilia and a rash, which started in the groins and lower abdomen 10 days after he was prescribed amoxicillin for a presumed chest infection. The rash consisted of small pinhead-sized non-follicular pustules on a background of erythema. The rash desquamated after 2 weeks leaving normal-looking background skin. Liver and kidney function tests were all within normal range. There was no mucosal involvement. What is the most llkel't diagnosis?
options: Drug reaction with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms.
questions.explanation:
The history and clinical findings are typical of AGEP (acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis) whieh is a self-limiting drug eruption that often begins in the flexlires.
Pustular psoriasis is the main differential but a history' of previous psoriasis and the absence of any drug intake can help differentiate the two conditions.
An eosinophilic infiltrate in the biopsy can sometimes be helpful and would point towards AGEP.
Acanthosis and papillomatosus are often seen in pustular psoriasis and rarely in AGEP, which can also aid in the differentiation.
Drug eruptions that are accompanied by fever include AGEP, toxic epidermal necrolysis/Stevens-Johnson syndrome and DRESS.

questions.stem: A 45-year-old man presents to the rheumatologist with severe psoriasis and joint pains. Which of the following is not a recognised form of psoriatic arthritis?
questions.explanation:
Psoriatic art.hropathy can present in the following forms:
-Distal int-erphal::ingeal joint (commonest).
-Ollgoarticular asymmetrical.
-Polyarticular symmetrical (rheumatoid arthritis like).
-Spondylitis and sacroiliitis.
-Arthritis mutilans.

questions.stem: A 55-year-old woman presents with a 5-week history of burning sensation of her feet. Weight bearing was extremely painful. The pain was only partially relieved on cold water soaks. Examination showed erythema of the soles of the feet which was very tender to touch. Pedal pulsations were normal. She had a history of duodenal ulceration for which she took omeprazole. Heamatological investigations showed hae moglobin of 12.Sg/dl, normal white cell and differential count and a platelet count of 550x103 /1. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation:
Erythromelalgia is characterised by intense burning pain and erythema (marked redness) of the extremities.
Erythromelalgia is classified into primary and secondary or early-onset and late-on set forms.
Primary erythromelalgia develops spontaneously and is also known as idiopathic erythromelalgia as the cause remains unknown.
Secondary erythromelalgia can be secondary to myeloproliferative disorders, neurological diseases (e.g. multiple sclerosis, peripheral neuropathy), or autoimmune diseases(e.g. lupus, diabetes mellitus).
The most common cause of secondary erythromelalgia are myeloproliferative disorders including polycythaemia vera, and essential thrombocythaemia.
Erythromelalgia may precede the diagnosis of myeloproliferative disorders in 85% of cases.
It is characterised by red, painful, warm hands or feet.
Chilblain-like lesions can occur in myeloproliferative disorders but are cold to touch.
The burning symptoms are exacerbated by warming or hanging the limb downward, and relieved with cooling and elevation.
Systemic treatments include aspirin, serotonin re-uptake inhibitors - venlafaxine, sertraline, fluoxetine, paroxetine; tricyclic antidepressants-amitriptyline, imipramine, gabapentin, nifedipine, diltiazem and prostaglandins-misoprostol.

questions.stem: A 58-year-old woman is admitted with deep vein thrombosis. Three days after being commenced on warfarin she develops necrotic and painful bullae on her thighs. What should be the next step in management?
questions.explanation:
Warfarin causes inactivation of clotting factors II, VII, IX and X and proteins C and 5.
Cond,tions such as inherited deticiency of protein C, protein S or factor V leidet1, mutations in methylene tetra hydro foiate reduc.tase gene causing hyperhomocysteinaemia, antithrombin 111 deficiency or the presence of antiphospholipid antibodies predispose to warfarin-induced skin necrosis.
The first step in management is to stop the warfarin therapy.
Other measures include administration of vitamin Kor protein C concentrates.

questions.stem: A 65-year-old patient presents with velvety pigmented changes in axillary skin and similar changes around the perioral area. You are worried that he may have an internal malignancy. Which of the following is the most common malignancy associated with these cutaneous changes?
questions.explanation:
Gastric cancer is the commonest tumour associated with malignant acanthosis nigricans.
The changes may regress if thetumour, usually an adenocarcinoma of the stomach or bowel, is removed.

questions.stem: A 55-year-old man is admitted to the hepatology ward and isundergoing investigations for jaundice. Your hepatologist colleague asks you to have a look at his nails, which display a bluish discolouration of the lanulae. Which of the following is associated with azure nails?
questions.explanation:
Azure lanulae, a bluish colour of the lanular portion of nails, occurs In hepatolenticular degeneration (Wilson's disease).
Similar nail changes and corneal changes resembling Wilson's Kayser-Fleischer rings may also be evident in patients with argyria or after treatment with busulfan or antimalarials.

questions.stem: A 45-year-old patient is diagnosed with Crohn's disease. He has apthous ulceration. Other cutaneous features of Crohn's disease include all of the following except:
questions.explanation:
Aphthous ulcers may be a presenting feature of Crohn's disease.
Oral granulomatous nodules are commonly seen in Crohn's disease, where they may coalesce to give a "cobblestone" appearance.
Granulomatous cheilitis may predate bowel disease by several years.
Granulomas may also occur in the perineum, at colostomy and ileostomy sites, and in association with scars, sinuses, and fistulas.
Granulomas can occur at sites not contiguous with the bowel, such as the trunk and limbs: the so-called "metastatic" cutaneous Crohn's disease.

questions.stem: A forensic pathologist is examining hair for suspected poisoning. Chronic exposure and cumulative toxicity of which of the following chemicals can be identified in this way?
questions.explanation:
Mercury intoxication can lead to hair loss with or without neurological symptoms.
Elevated mercury levels can be found in hair, blood, or urine.
Boric acid intoxir.ation also results in hair loss.
Gastrointestinal, central nervous system, and renal symptoms; a hemorrhagic diathesis; and exfoliation or bullae are also seen with boric acid intoxication.
Blood boric acid levels are elevated In affected patients.
Thallium poisoning leads to dramatic hair loss, with complete epilation occurring 2 to 3 weeks after intoxication.
Neurologic symptoms including irritability, dysesthesia, ataxia, convulsions, and coma can also result following thallium intoxication.
Blood and urine levels of thallium are positive at the time of acute poisoning.
In contrast to the above, arsenic exposure does not cause hair loss.
Arsenic concentrates in the hair, which facilitates a diagnosis long after intoxication may have occurred.
P0..70

questions.stem: A 12-year-old patient is diagnosed with alopecia areata. His parents are interested in knowing the prognosis. The following are associated with a poor prognosis in alopecia areata except:
questions.explanation:
Spontaneous remission is common in most patients with localised patches of alopecia areata.
Poor prognostic factors in alopecia areata include alopecia totalis and universalis, ophiasis pattern, onset in childhood, loss of body hair, nail involvement, atopy, and a positive family history for alopecia areata.

questions.stem: A 40-year-old man presents with androgenetic alopecia. He has heard about topical minoxidil solution. Which of the following statements regarding the use of topical minoxidil solution in androgenetic alopecia is not true?
options: Any hair gained is lost within 4 to 6 months of stopping minoxidil treatment.
Mean increase in hair density of 10-12% can be achieved.
Minoxidil is effective in treating vertex balding.
Minoxidil is not effective in treating frontotemporal recession.
questions.explanation:
Up to 60 percent of men show improvement in vertex balding using 5 % minoxidil lotion.
A mean increase in hair density of 10 to 12% is obtained.
The response rate with 2 % lotion are lower (the recommended concentration in women).
Any hair gained is lost within 4 to 6 months of stopping treatment.
Minoxidil is not effective in treating frontotemporal recession.

questions.stem: A 65-year-old man is seen with transverse depressions in nail plate. He has been undergoing cancer chemotherapy. Where does the abnormality originate?
questions.explanation:
Beau's lines result from a temporary arrest of proximal nail matrix proliferation.
These appear as transverse grooves in the nail plate that move distally with nail growth.
Multiple Beau's lines in the same nail indicates repetitive insults.
Beau's lines at the same level in several nails suggest a systemic cause.
The time of the insult leading to Beau's lines can be dated by measuring the distance of the groove from the proximal nail fold.
Causes of Beau's lines include local traurria, or can be related to local cutaneous dis ease, particularly eczema and paronychia.
Systemic causes include drugs (especially chemotherapy), high fever, viralillness, surgery, and peripheral ischemia.

questions.stem: You see a 35-year-old patient with longit1Jdinal melanonychia affecting 2 finger nails. Which of the following is not a recognised cause?
questions.explanation:
Melanonychia signifies the presence of melanin in the nail plate and appears as a single or longitudinal brown to black band.
Caused by activation or proliferation of nail matrix melanocytes.
Causes include racial, acquired immunodeficiency syndrome, inflammatory nail disorders, certain medications, Addison's disease, pregnancy, Laugier-Huntz;ker syndrome, and trauma.
Single nail melanonychia may be secondary to nail matrix naevus or melanoma.

questions.stem: A 60-year-old woman is referred with scaly, crusted erosions on the malar area of the face and seborrhoeic areas. Skin biopsy shows acantheilysis in the superficial epidermis just below the stratum corneum and in the granular layer. Antinuclear antibodies are detected on serological testing. Which of the following is the correct diagnosis?
questions.explanation:
Senear-llsher syndrome or pemphigus erythematosus is a localized form of pemphigus foliceous.
Scaly and crusted lesions occur across the malar area of the face and in other seborrheic areas.
Pemphigus erythematosus may remain localized for years, or it may evolve into more generalized pemphigus foliaceous.
Many patients with pemphigus erythematosus show serologic findings suggestive of systemic lupus erythematosus, especially the presence of anti-nuclear antibodies.

questions.stem: A 70-year-old man is admitted with painful stomatitis and a polymorphous cutaneous eruption with a predominantly blistering rash. A skin biopsy showed Intra-epidermal acantholysis and direct immunofluoresence showed deposition of immunoglobulin G and complement in the epidermal inteniellular space5, and granular/linear complement deposition along the epidermal basement membrane zone. Which of the following is the most common associated diagnosis?
questions.explanation:
Paraneoplastic pemphigus is an autoimmune disorder.
It is almost always linked to an underlying lymphoproliferative disorder. Its features include painful stomatitis and a polymorphous cutaneous eruption including blistering, lichenoid, erythema multiforme-like lesions. Histologic findings include acantholysis, lichenoid, or interface changes.
Direct immunofluorescence demonstrates deposition of immunoglobulinG (IgG) and complement in the epidermal intercellular spaces, and often granular/linear complement deposition along the epidermal basement membrane zone.
In addition to binding the cell surface of skin and mucosae in a pattern typical for pemphigus, serum auto-antibodies also bind to simple, columnar, and transitional epithelia.
These serum auto-antibodies identify desmogleins 1 and 3 and additionally desmoplakins, envoplakin, and periplakin.
Most commonly associated diseases include non-Hodgkin lymphoma (NHL), chronic lymphocytic leukemia, and Castleman's disease.

questions.stem: A 45-year-old patient who was commenced on lamotrigine for epilepsy presents with a morbilliform skin rash, fever, facial oedema and lymphadenopathy. Which of the following statements with regards to this drug reaction is incorrect?
options: Atypical lymphocytosis with subsequent eosinophilia may occur during the initial phases.
Central nervous system involvement is never seen.
Cross-reactivity to the other aromatic anticonvulsants may occur.
The reaction most frequently occurs on first exposure to the drug.
The susceptibility to develop this reaction may be familial.
questions.explanation:
Hypersensitivity syndrome reaction (HSR), also called drug reaction with eopsinophilia and systemtic symptoms (DRESS syndrome), is the presence of exarrthematous eruption in conjunction with fever and internal organ involvement (e.g. liver, kidney, central nervous system) which occurs in appoximateiy 1 in 3000 exposures to agents such as aromatic anti-convulsants, lamotrigine, sulfonamide antibiotics, dapsone, nitrofurantoin, nevirapine, minocycline, and allopurinol.
DRESS occurs most frequently on first exposure to the drug, with initial symptoms starting 1 to 6 weeks after exposure.
Fever and malaise are often the presenting symptoms.
Atypical lymphocytosis with subsequent eosinophilia may occur during the initial phases of the reaction in some patients.
Most patients have an exanthematous eruption.
Internal organ involvement can be asymptomatic.
The chemically reactive metabolites of aromatic anti-convulsants that a,e produced are detoxified by epoxidehydroxylases. If detoxification is defective, however, one of the metabolites may act as a hapten and initiate an immune response, stimulate apoptosis, or cause cell necrosis directly.
Approximately 70-75% of patients who develop anticonvulsant HSR in response to one aromatic anti-convulsant show cross-reactivity to the other aromatic anti-convulsants.
In vitro testing shows that there is a familial occurrence of HSR induced by anti-convulsants.
Thus, counselling of family members and disclosure of risk is essential.

questions.stem: A 34-year-old Asian man presents with a monomorphic pustular eruption on the face and limbs. Only a few papules and no comedones were seen. He was referred by the infectious diseases team, who had only recently commenced him on anti-tubercular therapy. Which of the following drugs is most commonly implicated?
questions.explanation:
Drug-induced acne may appear in atypical areas, such as on the arms and legs.
The lesions are mostly monomorphous and comedones are usually absent.
Topical tretinoin may be useful.
Implicated drugs include iodides, bromides, adrenocorticotropic hormone, glucocorticoids, isoniazid, androgens, and lithium.

questions.stem: Which of the following conditions c::in give a "pterygium" if the nail apparatus is affected?
questions.explanation:
V-shaped distal nick and leuko - or erythronychia can be seen in Darier's disease.
Lichen striatus may result in nail dystrophy and trachonychia but not pterygium.
Hyperthyroidism is associated with onycholysis.
Lichen nitidus is not associated with an'/ specific nail changes.

questions.stem: Which of the following conditions or eruptions is not considered paraneoplastic?
questions.explanation:
