Other paraneoplastic conditions include pruritus, acanthosis nigricans, Sweet's syn drome, Leser-Trelat sign, palmar tylosis, acquired hypertrichosis lanuginosa, migratory thrombophlebitis and paraneoplastic pemphigus.
Suspect malignancy in acanthosis nigricans in the presence of weight loss and nor moglycaemia.

questions.stem: Which pattern of drug eruptions is the commonest?
questions.explanation:
A maculo-papular drug exanthem is the commonest pattern of drug reaction occuring mostly within 2 weeks of drug ingestion.
Urticarial eruptions are the second most common followed by vasculitis.
Other patterns of drugeruptions include generalized exanthematous pustulosis, photosensitivity, lichenoid eruptions, xerosis, hair loss, bullous and exfoliative.
Some drugs can worsen existent skin diseases such as psoriasis.

questions.stem: Acquired ichthyosis can occur in which of the following?
questions.explanation:
Suddrm-onset of acquired ichthyosis should alert the dermatologist to look for an underlying malignancy.
Other causes include drugs and HIV infection.

questions.stem: Cutaneous sarcoidosis can clinically present as:
questions.explanation:
Plaque-type sarcoidosis is the commonest cutaneous type followed by nodules.
Other variants include ichthyotic, dystrophic nails, subcutaneous and scar sarcoidosis.

questions.stem: Which type of cryoglobulinaemia is not associated with hepatitis C infection?
questions.explanation:
Cryoglobulins are immunoglobulins that precipitate following cold exposure.
Types II and III are called mixed cryoglobulinaemia and can be associated with hepatitis C, connective tissue diseases, HIV, and lymphoproliferative disorders.
Type I is associated wih lymphoproliferative disorders but not with hepatitis C.
Suspect cryoglobulinaemia in the presence of a pernio-like appearance of digits, reticulate leukocytoclastic cutaneous vasculitis and when the levels of C4 are reduced.

questions.stem: In which of the following conditions can calcinosis cutis develop?
questions.explanation:
Calcinosis cutis is a well-recognized complication of juvenile dermatomyositis although it may occur (less commonly) in the adult form.
Juvenile dermatomyositis is not associated with an underlying malignancy (unlike the adult form).
Other conditions in which calcinosis cutis may occur include hyperparathyroidism, pseudohypoparathyroidi.;;m and chronic renal failure.

questions.stem: In which of the following is poikiloderma a feature?
questions.explanation:
Poikiloderma consists of pigmentary changes, atrophy and telangiectasia.
Other conditions in whichpoiklloderma may ooccur include mycosis fungoides, Rothmund-Thomspson syndrome and Bloom's syndrome.
Poikiloderma of Civatte is a benign finding secondary to the effects of ultraviolet radiation and fragrances - appearing on the sides of the neck.

questions.stem: Which of the following drugs is associated with acneiform eruption?
questions.explanation:
An acneiform eruption secondary to a drug typically presents with predominantly monomorphic papules and pustules with no comedones (excepting the pre-existing comedones).
Other drugs that can give such an eruption include corticosteroids, androgens, phenytoin, isoniazid, haloperidol and sirolimus.
The relatively new anti-cancer drugs (Epidermal Growth factor Receptor Antagonists)
can give in addition to an acneiform eruption; xerosis, alopecia, pyogenic granuloma-like lesions in the digits and paronychia.

questions.stem: A 56-year-old man w;th myeloid leukaemia developed deranged iiverflinction tests, diarrhoea and a maculo-papular eruption involving the palms and soles with marked follicular accentuation. This occured within 6G days following an allogenic bone-marrow transplantation. The most likely diagnosis here is:
questions.explanation:
Acute GVHD occurs within the first 100 days following an allogenic transplant tissue (mostly but not exclusively bone marrow) and typically presents with an exanthematous eruption most markedly on the palms and soles, hepatitis, diarrhoea and malaise.
Occasionally erythroderma followed by an exfoliation can occur giving a clinical picture similar to toxic epidermal necrolysis.
The most important differential diagnoses include a viral and drug-related exanthem and the eruption of lymphocyte recovery.

questions.stem: Which of the following alopecias is typically non-scarring?
questions.explanation:
Other causes of scarring alopecias include folliculitis Decalvans, erosive pustular dermatosis and pseudopelade.
Non-scarring alopecias include anagen effluvium, alopecia areata, loose anagen syndrome and syphilitic alopecia (patchy with a "moth-eaten" appearance).
In scarring alopecia the type of infiltrate (neutrophilic, lymphocytic or mixed) is also important pointer to the diagnosis.

questions.stem: Which of the following cutaneous manifestations can be associated with hepatitis C infection?
questions.explanation:
Hepatitis C infection can be associated with several cutaneous manifestations which include polyarteritis nodosa, lichen planus, erythema nodosum, cryoglobulinaemia (types II and III) and chronic urticaria.
Hepatitis B and C should always be looked for in the work-up of porphyria cutanea tarda.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the auto-antigen in dermatitis herpetiformis?
questions.explanation:
Epidermal transglutaminases is the dominant auto-antigen in dermatitis herpetiformis.
Collagen VII is the target in epidermolysis bullosa acquista, whilst BP 230 and 180 are the auto-antigens in bullous pemphigoid.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements regarding IgA in dermatitis herpetiformis (DH) is true?
options: Granular IgA deposits may also be seen in the skin of patients with epidermolysis bullosa acquisita.
IgA deposits are not seen in the skin of patients with isolated coeliac disease.
IgA deposits are uniformly intense throughout the skin.
IgA deposits may decrease after treatment with drugs.
Linear igAdeposits In normal-appearing skin isthe most reliable criterion for the diagnosis of DH.
questions.explanation:
Granular (or fibrillar) IgA deposits in dermal papillary tips of peri-lesional and uninvolved skin of patients is a typical finding in dermatitis herpetiformis.
IgA deposits have not been seen in the skin of patients with isolated coeliac: disease (without dermatitis herpetiformis).
IgA deposits in dermatitis herpetiformis are unaffected by treatment with drugs.
IgA deposits may decrease in intensity or disappear after long-term gluten-free diet.
IgA deposits are not uniformly intense throughout the skin.
These deposits may be more easily and intensely seen in normal-appearing peri-lesional skin.
IgA deposits may also be seen in the skin of patients with bullous pemphigoid, Hen och Schonlein purpura, and alcoholic liver disease, although the patterns of distribution is different than those seen in dermatitis herpetiformis.

questions.stem: A 55-year-old diabetic woman presents with tense serous bullae on the lower legs. There is no perilesional erythema. Which of the following statements is correct?
options: Direct immunofluoresence shows IgG and C3 at the dermo-epidermal junction.
There is a direct correlation with glycaemic control.
questions.explanation:
Bullous disease of diabetes (bullosis diabeticorum) is a spontaneous, non-inflammatory, blistering condition of acral skin in patients with diabetes mellitus.
The aetiology is obscure and a history of antecedent trauma is not always forthcoming.
Many patients have associated nephropathy or neuropathy.
Tense, non-tender blisters are seen on non-erythematous, non-urticated areas of the feet or lower legs. Other involved sites include the fingers, toes, hands, arms and rarely, non-acral sites may be involved.
Histology is non-specific and immunofluorescence is negative.
The blister may be in subcorneal, intraepidermal, or subepidermal location.ihe condition is self-limiting and the blisters heal spontaneously within 2-6 weeks of onset.

questions.stem: A 60-year-old woman presents with a non-tender violaceous annular plaque on the dorsum of her hand. She is taking methotrexate for rheumatoid arthritis. A skin biopsy shows palisaded granulomas associated with necrobiosis and increased deposition of dermal mucin. Which one of the following statements regarding thiscondition is true?
options: Increasing the dose of methotrexate may improve the skin lesions.
Spontaneous resolution can be expected in 2 years.
The disease follows severity of rheumatoid arthritis.
There is an association with rheumatoid arthritis.
questions.explanation:
The clil"ical features and histology are typical of granuloma annulare (GA).
GA most commonly affects the dorsum of hands and feet.
GA can. present as subcutaneous, perforating, disseminated and the rare "in terstitial" variants.
Localised forms of GA are generally not associated with systemic illnesses.
Disseminated GA may be associated with diabetes mellitus.
Localised GA tends to resolve spontaneously (80% clearance in 2 years).
Disseminated GA lasts longer.
Potent topical and intralesional corticosteroids are the treatment of choice for localised lesions.
Phototherapy can be used in disseminated GA.

questions.stem: A 55-year-old patient presents with asymptomatic, firm, subcutaneous nodules on the elbow. A skin biopsy shows palisading granulomas with macrophages surrounding the eosinophilic fibrinoid degeneration of the collagen in the deep dermis. Which of the following is the most likely associated systemic disorder?
questions.explanation:
Rheumatoid nodules are most commonly seen on the elbows.
Other common sites include the extensor surfaces of the fingers.
Achilles tendon, ischial tuberosities and sacrum.They occur in 25%of patients with rheumatoid arthritis.

questions.stem: A 70-year-old woman is admitted with chronic renal failure. She develops gangrenous areas on her thighs. A skin biopsy shows calcific deposits in blood vessels, necrosis and panniculitis. Which of the following statements is true?
options: Intravenous sodium thiosulphate may bring about resolution.
Primary hyperparathyroidism is the aetiological factor.
Prognosis is excellent with spontaneous improvement in most.
Serum calcium levels are generally low.
questions.explanation:
Calciphylaxis or calcific uraemic arteriolopathy refers to calcification affecting small blood vessels.
Secondary hyperparathyroidismresults in high or normal levels of serum calcium and phosphate results in spreading skin necrosis.
Purple mottling is followed by painful skin ulceration.
Management includes restricting calcium and phosphate in diet and using a lower dialysate calcium concentration.
Bisphosponates and intravenous infusions of sodium thiosulfate have been used successfully.

questions.stem: A 44-year-old woman is admitted with fever, chest and hip pains, and a recurrent non-pruritic urticarial eruption that lasts for few hours and coincides with febriie episodes. Haematological investigations show raised erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) and C-React'.va Protein (CRP) and serum IgM. A skin biopsy shows perivascular neutrophilic inflammation. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation:
Features of Schnitzler's syndrome include chronic non-pruritic urcicaria, monoclonal IgM gammopathy, intermittent fever, asthenia, arthralgia, and bone pain with imaging evidence of osteosclerosis.
Biological findings usually include an increase in white blood cell count, ESR and CRP, which reflect an inflammatory syndrome and the presence of the monoclonal IgM.
Skin biopsy findings often include mononuclear or neutrophilic perivascular infiltrates.
Treatment with NSAIDs, dapsone, colchicine alone is usually unsatisfactory.
Recently Anakinra, an interleukin-1 receptor antagonist has been found to be an effective treatment.

questions.stem: A 45-year-old presents with widespread chronic plaque psoriasis. He also complains of joint pains. Radiological examination confirmed psoriatic arthritis. What is the commonest type of psoriatic arthritis?
questions.explanation:
Up to 30% patients with psoriasis suffer from psoriatic arthritis.
The five types of psoriatic arthritis are:
Asymmetric - affects 60-70%- commonly involves fingers or toes.
Symmetric polyarthritis -15% - resembles rheumatoid arthritis.
Distal interphalengeal joint disease - 5%
Destructive arthritis (arthritis mutilans) - 5%
Axial arthritis - 5% - resembles ankylosing spondylitis.

questions.stem: A 60-year-old man is admitted with an erythematous and scaly rash covering 95% of his body surface area. He is feeling cold and shivery and is noted to have generalised lymphadenopathy. What is the commonest cause of erythroderma overall?
questions.explanation:
This patient has erythroderma which by definition is involvement of >90% bod·f surface area with an erythematous and scaly rash.
The cause remains unknown in the majority of cases (30%).
Where a cause can be found, drug reactions are most commonly implicated.
Pre-existing skin diseases like atopic dermatitis and psoriasis, lymphoma and contact dermatitis are other causes of erythroderma.
130

questions.stem: A 75-year-old man presents with recurrent crops of small, pruritic blisters on the scalp, face and neck. Examination shows atrophic scars and small vesicles on the scalp. There was no involvement of oral mucosa. A punch biopsy shows a non-inflammatory, subepidermal blister and direct immunofluoresence demonstrates linear deposits of complement C3 and IgG at the dermo-epidermal junction. What is the diagnosis?
questions.explanation:
Brunsting-Perry cicatritial pemphigoid is a rare variant of cicatritial pemphigoid.
It is most commonly seen in elderly males.
Clinical features include pruritic, recurrent crops of vesicles which heal with atrophic scars.
The vesicles are confined mainly to the head and neck.
Histopathology shows subepidermal blisters with prominent perivascular infiltrates of lymphocytes, polymorphonuclears, eosinophils and prominent fibrosis in late stages.
Direct immunofluoresence shows staining with IgG and C3.
Successful treatments include dapsone and sulphamethoxypyridazine.

questions.stem: A 70-year-old man is admitted with weight loss and fatigue. He is noted to have ichthyosis. A computed tomography scan showed mediastinal lymphadenopathy. You make a diagnosis of acquired ichthyosis. Which of the following is not a recognised cause of acquired ichthyosis?
questions.explanation:
Acquired ichthyosis is associated with malignancies (especially Hodgkin's lymphoma), non-Hodgkin lymphoma, mycosis fungoides, myeloma, Kaposi's sarcoma, leiomyos11rcoma, and carcinomas of the lung, breast, ovary, and cervix.
Sarcoidosis, leprosy, thyroid disease, hyperparathyroidism, nutritional disorders, chronic renal failure, bone marrow transplantation, and HIV infection can all cause ichthyosis.
Auto-immune diseases, including systemic lupus erythematosus and dermatomyositis.
Medications - nicotinic acid, triparanol, butyrophenones, dixyrazine, cimetidine, and clofazimine.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is incorrect regarding auto-inflammatory syndromes?
options: Abdominal pain is common in acute attacks.
Arthralgia is common in acute attacks.
Fever is often present in acute attacks.
Raised inflammatory markers are almost always seen in acute attacks.
The predominant skin eruption during acute attacks consists of a maculopapular exanthem.
questions.explanation:
Auto-inflammatory syndromes are characterised by the presence of fever, abdominal pain, arthralgia and an urticarial eruption during acute attacks.
Raised inflammatory markers are almost always found during acute attacks. Its absence almost always excludes the presence of an auto-inflammatory syndrome.
These syndromes represent dysfunction of the innate immunity (neutrophils and macrophages) in the absence of auto-antibodies.
Examples of auto-inflammatory syndromes include hyper IgD syndrome, Schnitzler's syndrome, cryopyrin-associated-periodic-fever syndrome, TNF-receptor-associatedperiodic fever-syndrome (TRAPS) and familial Mediterranean fever.

questions.stem: Which of the following drugs is most likely to cause systemic vasculitis due to the induction of p-ANCA?
questions.explanation:
All the above listed drugs can result in positive p-ANCA with or without systemic vasculitis.
Propylthiouracil is an anti-thyroid drug most commonly associated with the induction of systemic vasculitis through p-ANCA which can occur several months to years following initiation of therapy.
Other causes of positive p-ANCA Include inflammatory bowel disease, rheumatoid arthritis andtuberculosis.

questions.stem: Which of the following is least likely to result in generalized pustular psoriasis?
questions.explanation:
Generalized pustular psoriasis is a dermatological emergency In which patients are often very unwell.
Leukocytosis and fever may be present.
Ultraviolet-A radiation, withdrawal of steroid therapy, crude coal tar and pregnancy can all trigger generalized pustular psoriasis.
It is worth checking calcium levelsin pustular psoriasis as hypocalcaemia may result in therapy resistance.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is correct?
options: Both heparin and warfarin-induced skin necrosis are related to the production of specific antibodies against the drugs.
Heparin-inducedskin necrosis is related to a drop in protein C levels.
Heparin-induced skin necrosis is related to the production of antibodies and therefore should never be re-challenged.
Warfarin -induced skin necrosis is related to the production of antibodies and therefore should never be re-challenged.
Warfarin-induced skin necrosis is a late manifestation of warfarin therapy, often occurring after the first six weeKS.
questions.explanation:
Warfarin-induced skin necrosis often occurs between day three and eight following initiation of warfarin due to the transient pro-coagulant state secondary to a drop in protein(s) C and S levels.
Heparin-inducedskin necrosis occurs due to the production of antibodies and should therefore never be re-challenged with heparin, unlike warfarin which can be re-challenged provided there is concomitant use of low molecular weight heparin in the initial phase.

questions.stem: 5-alpha-reductase is responsible for which type of hair loss?
questions.explanation:
5-alpha-reductase converts testosterone to the more potent dihydrotestosterone which is responsible for hair loss in androgenetic alopecia.
Finasteride is a drug that blocks this enzyme; hence it can be used in male pattern alopecia.
Thyroid disease and iron deficiency anaemia can contribute to diffuse hair loss in a non-scarring fashion such as telogen effluvium.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements regarding the diagnosis of hidradenitis suppurativa is incorrect?
options: Arthritis can be a manifestation in severe cases.
Obesity tends to worsen the condition.
Smoking tends to worsen the condition.
There is increased risk of basal cell carcinoma.
questions.explanation:
There is increased risk of squamous cell carcinoma in patients with hidradenitis suppurativa due to the chronic inflammation.
Lymphoedema is also a complication of the disease.
Lithium tends to exacerbate hidradenitis suppurat.iva.
The condition can be associated with inflammatory bowel disease, pyoderma gangrenosum, spondylc::irthropathy and SAPHO syndrome.

questions.stem: Naso-septaI perforation can be found in all of the following except?
questions.explanation: Bevacizumab is a humanised monoclonal anti-angiogenic antibody used in the treatment for various cancers. Cocnine use, Wegener's granulomatosis, trauma and bevacizumab have all been associated with naso-septal perforation.

questions.stem: Which of the following is not a treatment option in pruritus secondary to endstage renal failure?
questions.explanation:
Pruritus is a common feature of end-stage renal disease and treatment depend on the severity.
Treatments include topical anti-pruritic therapy, UVB phototherapy, gabapentin and the use of selective neuro-epinephrine re-uptake inhibitors such as minazapine.
Rifampicin is used in pruritus secondary to chronic liver disease as it induces liver enzymes.
Other treatments for chronic liver disease inclucle the use vf mirtazapine or paroxetine, bile acid resins and naltrexone.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the most common manifestation of ocular rosacea?
questions.explanation:
Rosacea has four sub-types - erythematotelangiectatic, papulo-pustular, phymatous and ocular rosacea.
Ocular rosacea can be found in half of the patients, which is more frequently associ ated with the papulo-pustular variant.
Meibomian gland dysfunction is the commonest manifestation of ocular rosacea leading to dry eyes.

questions.stem: Which type of cryoglobulinaemia is least likely to be assoc,ated with smallve.;sel vasculitis?
questions.explanation:
Type-1 cryoglobulinaemia is often associated with monoclonal gammopathy and occlusion of small blood vessels but rarely small vessel vasculitis.
Cryoglobulinaemia types-2 and 3 are called essential mixed cryoglobulinaemia and can be associated with hepatitis C and other infections. It can be associated with small vessel vasculitis.
Type-2 cryoglobulinaemia can in some cases be associated with monoclonal gammopathy.

questions.stem: A 52-year-old woman presented with a 3-year history of multiple painful and tender nodular lesions involving the upper aspects of her arms 2nd thighs, which were followed by atrophic scarring of the affected areas. She also suffered from chronic arthralgia and myalgia. She had positive ANA and weak double-stranded DNA antibodies. A biopsy showed evidence of atrophic epidermis with peri-vascular lymphocytic infiltrate, lobular panniculitis with a lymphocytic infiltrate. The most likely diagnosis is?
questions.explanation:
Lupus profundus is also known as lupus panniculitis, which is a chronic relapsing pannicullitis that occurs in 1 - 3% of patients with cutaneous lupus erythematosus, affecting mostly women.
Clinically, this can present with tender subcutaneous nodules and plaques with a predilection for the upper aspects of arms, shoulders and buttocks.
Histologically, it affects the cutaneous fat in a lobular fashion.
Treatment is with systemic steroids, hydroxychloroquine, dapsone, azathioprine or thalidomide.
Systemic retinoids are often unhelpful in thiscondition.
Erythema nodosum affects mostly the shins. Histologically, this is characterised by a septal panniculitis.
Lupus pernio is a term used for a variant of cutaneous sarcoidosis affecting the nose or ears resembling a frost bite.

questions.stem: Frusemide is a loop diuretic that is widely used. Which of the following blistering disorders can be caused by this drug?
questions.explanation:
Vancomycin is the commonest cause of linear IgA disease.
Penicillamine and ACE inhibitors are common causes of drug-induced pemphigus.
Pseudo-porphyria can also be caused by thiazide diuretics and non-steroidal antiinflammatory drugs.

questions.stem: Which of the following conditions is not an acantholytic disorder?
questions.explanation:
Bullous pemphigoid is a blistering disease which is subepidermal and acantholysis does not take place.
Hailey-Hailey and Darier's diseases are both inherited forms of acantholytic disorders.
Grover's disease is also known as transient acantf-iolytic dematosis and often pre sents with discrete pruritic papules and vesicles often on the back of middle aged or elderly people.

questions.stem: A 53-year-old man developed an intensely pruritic eruption consisting of violar.eous papules on his trunk and limbs with some follicular accentuation. He received a bone-marrow transplant four months prior to the onset of the eruption. Which of the following statements regarding this condition is incorrect?
options: A lichenoid drug eruption is the differential diagnosis in this case.
In grade 4 of the disease the histological appearances can resemble those of toxic epidermal necrolysis.
The chronic variant always follows on from the acute setting.
The condition is primarily mediated by T lymphocyt s.
The incidence is highest in the setting of bone marrow transplantation.
questions.explanation:
Chronic graft-versus-host-disease generally develops 3 months after transplantation and many not occur after the acute variant of the disease.
The condition is most likely to develop in the setting of allogeneic, unmatched and unrelated donor.
The 2 variants of the chronic form include lichenoid and sclerodermoid.
Advanced age, male gender and the presence of HLA-DR4 allele in the recipient are all risk factors for the development of the condition.

questions.stem: A 64-year-old man with 3-year history of dermatomyositis presented with firm, painful nodules on his abdomen and limbs. Histology showed evidence of calicification in the dermis. The most likely mechanism here is:
questions.explanation:
Pathologic calcification of cutaneous tissue can be dystrophic, metastatic or idiopathic.
Oystrophk calcinosis cutis consists of deposition of calcium salts in abnormal or damaged tissue, mostly elastic fibres, and occurs in the setting of normal serum calcium levels particularly in connective ti sue disorders.
Metastatic calcinosis cutis occurs in the setting of hypercalcaemia and involves the calcification of normal tissues.
Idiopathic caicinosis cu-tis consists of calcification of normal tissues in the setting of normal calcium levels.
Primary osteoma cutis can occur in the setting of Albright's hereditary osteodystrophy, fibrodysplasiaossificans progressiva and progressive osseous heteroplasia.
Secondary osteoma cutis may occur following previous dermatoses such as military osteoma cutis on the face secondary to acne vulgaris.

questions.stem: A 40-year-old woman recently diagnosed with acute myeloid leukaemia presented 3 weeks following treatment with thechemotherapy agent cytarabine. Clinically she had pruritic and tender papules on her forearms and chest with bilateral palmar erythema. The papules were slightly oedematous and some nave coalesced to form plaques. A biopsy taken from one of the papules showed a dense neutrophilic infiltrate around eccrine glands with associated necrosis. Which of the following statements regarding thiscondition is incorrect?
options: Acute myeloid leukaemia is the most common associated malignancy with this condition.
Cytarabine is the commonest reported chemotherapy agent respom,ible for thiscondition.
The condition is associated with a high mortality rate and future chemotherapy should be avoided.
The condition is self-limiting and treatment is often not required.
The condition usually begins within 3 weeks following chemotherapy.
questions.explanation:
Neutrophilic eccrine hidradenitis is a self-limiting condition occurring mostly within 3 weeks of cytarabine in the treatment of acute myeloid leukaemia.
Other chemotherapy agents that have been reported to cause the condition include bleomycin, cyclor,,hosphamide and doxorubicin.
Systemic steroids and dapsone have been used in cases where the lesions are very painful and oedematous.
Dapsone has been reported to be used successfully as prophylactic therapy.

questions.stem: In which of the following subtypes of vasculitis is the presence of granulomas a feature?
questions.explanation:
Granulomas are also present in Wegener's granulomatosis but In Churg-Strauss there it. often tissue eosinophilia as well.
In erythema elevatum diutinum the infiltrate is predominantly neutrophilic with areas of fibrosis (in chronic case).
In granuloma faciale there are no granulomas but a Grenz zone is present separating the dermis from the epidermis.
In cryoglobulinaemia a homogenous eosinophilic material is found within blood vessels.

questions.stem: A 40-year-old man with a history of excesive alcohol intake and self-neglect has a 12-month history of intermittent scaling of his hands and feet associated with a malar rash on his cheeks and a powdery scale on his nose. In addition, he had marked erythema of his tongue and has been complaining of loose stools for several months. He scores low on mini mental state examination, The most likely diagnosisis:
questions.explanation:
Pellagra is classically a disease of the "4 Os": dermatitis, diarrhoea, dementia and death.
It is due to deficiency in vitamin 83 (Niacin).
Pellagra typically spares the nails and hair and can also be caused by deficiency in tryptophan.
Photosensitivity is often present.
6-Mercaptopurine, isoniazid and 5-flurouracil are drugs that can in rare cases cause pellagra.
Beriberi is due to deficiency in vitamin 81 (Thiamine) and typically gives ore-genital dermatitis with encephalopathy, cardiac failure and peripheral neuropathy.

questions.stem: The phenomenon by which gentle pressure on an intact bulla forces the fluid to spread under the skin away from the site of pressure in pemphigus is known as:
questions.explanation:
Due to the lack of cohesion within the epidermis, its upper layers easily move later ally with slight pressure or rubbing in patients with active pemphigus. This is known as Nlkolsky's sign.
The bulla-spread phenomenon is when gentle pressure on an intact bulla forces the fluid to spread under the skin away from the site of pressure (Asboe-Hansen's sign, also referred to as the 'indirect Nikolsky' or 'Nlkolsky II' sign).

questions.stem: A patient presents with scaly and crusted lesions on the malar region of the face and in other 'seborrhoeic' areas. Direct immunofluoresence shows in vivo IgG and C3 deposition on cell surfaces of keratinocytes as well as the basement membrane zone. Serology shows presence of circulating antinuclear antibodies. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation:
Pemphigus erythematosus is a localized variant of pemphigus foliaceus.
Scaly and crusted lesions of pemphigus foliaceus are seen on the malar region of the face and in seborrhoeic distribution.
The term 'pemphigus erythematosus' describes patients with immunologic features of both lupus erythematosus and pemphigus, i.e. in vivo IgG and C3 deposition on cell surfaces of keratinocytes as well as the basement membrane zone, in addition to circulating antinuclear antibodies.

questions.stem: Use of antigen specific ELISA allows for diagnosis of pemphigus. Which of the following best describes ELISA for pemphigus?
options: Serum is positive against Dsgl but negative against Dsg3 in mucosaldominant type of pemphigus vulgaris.
Serum is positive against Dsglbut negative against Dsg3 in pemphigus vulgaris.
Serum is negative against both Dsgl and Dsg3 in mucocutaneous type of pemphigus vulgaris.
questions.explanation:
Patients' serum is tested on ELISA plates pre-coated with recombinant Dsgl or Dsg3 protein leading to detection of specific antibodies against Dsgl or Dsg3.
In pemphigus foliaceus the serum is positive against Dsgl but negative against Dsg3.
In mucosal-dominant type of pemphigus vulgaristhe serum is negative against Dsgl but positive against Dsg3.
In mucocutaneous type of pemphigus vulgaris the serum is positive against both Dsgl and Dsg3.
ELISA scores demonstrate parallel fluctuations with disease activitv and are useful in monitoring disease activity.

questions.stem: Which of the following virus is not been known to be associated with lichen planus (LP)?
questions.explanation:
,., In several case-control studies, the prevalence of HC.V was higher in patients with LP than in controls. This association seems to be strongest in Japanese and Mediterranean populations.
,., Of the various types of LP, it is the oral form that is most commonly viewed as a manifestation of HCV infection.
,.,Transfusion-transmitted virus (TTV) Is highly prevalent in patients with liver diseases, Including those with chronic HCV infection. Direct role of TTV In causation of lichen planus is lacking.
,., By in situ hybridization and immunohistochemical techniques, HHV-6 was detected in 67-100% of oral LP lesions and it was absent from normal oral tissues.
,., HHV7 DNA has been demonstrated in lesional samples of lichen planus more often than non leslonal LP.

questions.stem: One of the following is not useful in differentiating lichen striatus from linear lichen planus (LP):
options: Histology shows lichenoid changes in lichen planus.
Hypopigmentation is more often a sequlae of lichen striatus.
Lichen planus often results in hyperpigmentation.
Pruritus is more commonly a feature of lichen planus.
Spontaneous resolution occurs within a short period of time in lichen striatus.
questions.explanation:
,., Differential diagnoses of lichen striatus include linear porokeratosis, linear psoriasis, inflammatory linear verrucous epidermal nevus, linear Darrier's disease, linear LP, blaschkitis and linedr GVHD.
,., Linear LP and lichen striatus can occasionall'ybe indistinguishable histologicaliy.
,.,Hypopigmentation is a frequent sequela of lichen striatus.
,.,Hyperpigmentation appears more commonly associated with LP.
,., Lichen striatus is also characterized by minimal, if any, pruritus, unlike lichen planus which can be very pruritic.
,., Spontaneous resolution occurs within a short period of time In lichen striatus.

questions.stem: Of all the pregnancy associated dermatoses, cholestasis of pregnancy is associated with highest incidence of fetal distress. The risk of fetal distress is highest if levels of maternal bile salts are higher than:
questions.explanation:
Cholestasis of pregnancy is defined by:
Generalized pruritus, with or without jaundice.
Absence of viral or drug induced hepatitis.
Absence of primary lesions.
Biochemical abnormalities consistent with cholestasis.
Disappearance of signs and symptoms following pregnancy.
Recurrence during subsequent gestation(s) and oestrogen containing oralcontra-ceptives is common.
Levels of maternal bile salts above 40 µmol/1 are correlated with an increased incidence of fetal (but not maternal) complicatior,s.
Meconium staining and premature labor occur in as many as 45% of patients.

questions.stem: The case of a 23-year-old female medical student, who has recently returned from an elective in Bhutan, is discussed at your local dermato-pathology meeting. She presented with scaly plaques over the shoulders and upper arms alongside systemic upset. Diagnostic skin biopsy demonstrated sarcoidal granuloma, with no plasma cell infiltrate. Both serum ACE and chest radiography have proved reassuring. What next step investigation will likeiy be suggested?
questions.explanation:
Sarcoidal or naked granulomas consist of loose groupings of epitheloid histiocytes, giant cells and lymphocytes.
Asteroid bodies may also be seen within the cytoplasm of macrophages.
Differential diagnoses include sarcoidosis and Crohn's disease. Once sarcoidosis has been excluded, colonoscopy would be warranted to exclude metastatic cutaneous Crohn's disease.
Secondary syphilis can present with sarcoidal granulomas but the absence of plasma cells points away from this diagnosis.
Mycobacterium tuberculosis granulomas classically occur with caseous necrosis.

questions.stem: A 38-year woman is seen in clinic with extensively sun-damaged skin. She points out well-demarcated and entirely asymptomatic areas of fine paper-like wrinklingover her trunk andupper arms that she first noted during a recent pregnancy. No evidence of transepithelial elimination of elastic fibres or fib;osis are seen on diagnostic skin biopsy. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation:
Mid-dermal elastolysis is a rare, acquired, skin condition.
Focal loss of elastic fibres results from increased elastase enzyme activity.
Its exact cause is unknown but associations include ultraviolet radiation, pregnancy and the oral contraceptive pill.
..,It most commonly presents with well-demarcated areas of fine wrinkling but can also manifest with perifollicular papules of reticular erythema.
Transepithelial elimination of elastic fibres is a histological feature characteristic of eiastosis perforans serpiginosa, a condition associated with both Ehlers-Dantos syndrome and pseudoxanthoma elasticum. Other associations include Down's syndrome, Marfan syndrome, osteogenesis imperfecta, scleroderma, and D-penicillamine.
.., Dermal fibrosis is seen in scarring disorders such as acrodermatitis chronica atrophicans (which also demonstrates dermal atrophy) and cutaneous morphea.
Acrodermatitis chronica atrophicans is associated with Lyme's disease.

questions.stem: You are asked to review a patient who has developed highly itchy tense blisters around her umbilicus. She is 5 days post-partum and presented with a similar problem after delivery of her first child. You review the histology report a skin biopsy taken at the time. What direct IMf pattern do you anticipate?
options: Linear IgG and C3 at DEJ.
questions.explanation:
Pemphigoid gest;;tionis occurs with an incidence of approximately 1 In 50,000 in those patients with high risk (DR3 or DR4) HLA types.
Other risk factors include a personal history of the disease, Caucasian heritage and other autoimmune disease. There is also a recognised association with choriocarcinoma and hydatidiform moles.
The target antigen concerns bullous pemphigoid antigen 2 (BP180).
Presentation may rarely be in the first trimester but is more typically in the second or third trimester or post-partum, as here. An important clinical clue is that the itchy lesions commonly start around the umbilicus, before spreading the rest of the torso and other areas such as the intertriglnous areas and extremities. The face, palms and soles are usually spared. Mucosal involvement occurs In fewer than 20% of cases
Diagnosis is with skin biopsy.
H&E analysis demonstrates an identical pattern to bullous pemphigoid, with split at the DEJ.
Direct IMFshows linear C3 in all cases, with additional IgG only seen in approximately 25% of cases.
This contrasts to bullous pemphigoid where the typical pattern on direct IMF is linear IgG and C3 deposition

questions.stem: What perr.entage of patients with linear IgA disease have oral mucous membrane involvement?
questions.explanation:
Linear IgA disease is the commonest autoimmune bullous disease in children.
It usually arises spontaneously but sometimes a triggering infection can beidentified.
The classic presentation is with an annular or crown-of-jewels configuration
In adults, the most common association is with medication, especially vancomydn.
Other associations include inflammatory bowel disease, rheumatological disorders and both haematological and non-haernatologica: malignancy.
On skin biopsy, the H&Esection demonstrates a:;ub-epidermal splitwith neutrophilic infiltrate in a linear fashion, and direct IMF demonstrates linear IgA deposition. This contrasts to dermatitis herpetiformis, where granular neutrophils predominate
The treatment of choice, as with many other IgA-associated neutrophilic disorders, is Dapsone.
Second line agents include sulfapyridine

questions.stem: Ophiasis is recognised to be a poor prognostic marker in alopecia areata. What pattern of hair loss doses it describe?
questions.explanation: Other poor prognostic markers in alopecia areata include: DQ7 or DR3 haplotype, family history, early/childhood onset, associated atopy (especially with fillagrin gene mutation) or autoimmune disease, extensive hair loss, nail disease (especially dystrophy) and chronicity.

questions.stem: You suspect drug-related Churg-Strauss syndrome in a patient you nave oeen treating for chronic urticaria. Which class of drug is likely implicated?
questions.explanation:
Use of montelukast, a leukotriene receptor inhibitor, is c:1ssociated with a higher incidence of Churg-Strauss syndrome. As with non-drug-related cases, p-ANCA levels can be elevated.
Calcineurin inhibitors include ciclosporin (which first must form a complex with cyclophilin-A)
Calcineurin inhibition prevents migration of the NFAT transcription factor into the T-celi nucleus and ultimately results in IL-2 signalling inhibition.
The Anti-IgE monoclonal antibody omallzumab has recently been granted a lice;ice for use as a second-line agent for treatment refractory chronic spontaneous urt;caria

questions.stem: Which of the following medications would you wish to avoid in a patient with urticarial pigmentosa?
questions.explanation:
Other medicines that may trigger mast cell degranulation, and thereby worsen mast cell mediated conditions such as urticarial pigmentosa, include: Amphotericin B, neuromuscular blocking agents such as gallamine, opiates, NSAIDs and aspirin, dextran plasma expander, polymyxin B, quinine and reserpine.
The other medications listed are more classically associated with triggering or worsening psoriasis.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements regarding Raynaud's phenomenon is correct?
options: Digital skin colour changes are in the order of red, white, then blue.
Ergot compounds used in anti-migraine medications improve the condition.
This is most commonly seen in patients with systemic lupus erythematosus
This is most commonly seen in patients with systemic sclerosis.
This is often associated with interstitial lung disease in the presence of connective tissue disease.
questions.explanation:
Raynaud's phenomenon is most commonly seen in systemic sclerosis, followed by systemic lupus erythematosus and Sjogren's syndrome.
The typical digital skin colour changes are white, followed by blue, then red.
Ergot compounds, bleomycin, cisplatin and beta blockers tend to worsen this phenomenon.
Mechanics hands are seen in dermatomyositis and affect the lateral aspects of the digits. There is a strong association with interstitial lung disease.

questions.stem: A 62-year-old man with a background of rheumatoid arthritis presented with redto-brown plaques and nodules on the dorsal aspect of his hands, which have been present for two months. These are mostly asymptomatic and tend to appear on the metacarpophalangeal joints. Full skin examination showed similar plaques and nodules on both his elbows. There are no associated nail changes. Which of the following statements regarding this condition is incorrect?
options: Histology from these lesions typically shows leukocytoclastic vasculitis.
Systemic steroids often result in complete resolution of the lesions.
The condition can be seen in HIV infected patients.
The condition responds well to treatment with dapsone therapy.
This condition can be associated with IgA monoclonal gammopathy.
questions.explanation:
The diagnosis here is erythema elevatum diutinum and can be associated with several haematological abnormalities, including IgA monoclonal gammopathy, myelodys plastic syndrome and multiple myeloma.
The condition responds generally well to dapsone therapy and poorly to systemic steroids.
Histology typically shows leukocytoclastic vasculitis with a neutrophilic infiltrate, which may mimic Sweet's syndrome and rheumatoid nodule histologically. In chronic stages, fibrosis and cholesterol deposits are often found.

questions.stem: A 41-year-old Caucasian man presented with a three-year history of yellow papules coalescing into symmetrical plaques on the axillae, groin and the peri-orbital skin. A biopsy from two separate lesions showed dermal infiltrate with polymorphic cells consisting of foamy histiocytes, which stained negative for CD1a and positive for CD68 and factor XIII. Based on the clinical and histological features, you diagnose xanthomata disseminatum. Which of the following statements regarding this condition is incorrect?
options: Rectal mucosal biopsy is often unhelpful.
The condition responds poorly to topical steroids.
Lipid profile is often normal in these patients.
This condition forms part of the Langerhans' cell histiocytosis.
questions.explanation:
Xanthomata disseminatum is a non-Langerhans cell histiocytosis and stains negative for both S100 and CD1a - markers of Langerhans cells.
Foamy histiocytes and the presence of Touton giant cells are often observed.
The condition often has normal lipid profile and may be associated with diabetes insipidus due to pituitary involvement.
A rectal mucosal biopsy can be helpful in cases of systemic amyloidosis.
Treatment of xanthomata disseminatum is often challenging although agents such as azathioprine, cyclophosphamide and carbon dioxide laser have been used.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements regarding pityriasis lichenoides chronica is correct?
options: Histologically, this has 3 similar appearance to pityriasis lichenoides et varioliformis Acuta (PLEVA).
Phototherapy can be useful in this condition.
The condition appears predominantly on the face and neck.
The lesions tend to heal with significant pitted scarring.
Transformation to cutaneous lymphoma never occurs
questions.explanation:
Eruotions of pityriasis lichenoides chronica are characterised by erythematous to brown macules or slightly raised papules with fine centrally adherent scale "mica scale".
Histologically, the appearance is slightly different than PLEVA, which is characterised by a superficial lymphocytic infiltrate, mild parakeratosis and minimal aoptotickerat inocytes. The granular layer is often preserved.
Transformation to cutaneous lymphomas has been documented in some cases.
This condition tends to affect young adults and is predominantly found on the trunk and upper extremities.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements regarding eosinophilic cellulitis (Well's syndrome) is correct?
options: Dapsone is the first line treatment.
Flame figures are pathognomonic of this condition.
Peripheral eosinophilia is extremely common and is found in almost all cases.
The condition is often progressive with no spontaneous resolution.
Vasculitis is absent on histology and direct immunofluoresence is negative.
questions.explanation:
Systemic corticosteroids are the first line treatment of choice in Well's syndrome.
Spontaneous resolution often occurs.
Flame figures are found in other eosinophil-mediated dermatoses such as allergic contact dermatitis, bullous pemphigoid and insect biteo:.
Peripheral eosinophilia is found in almost half of the cases.
The presence of Peripheral eosinophilia and organ damage should raise the suspicion of hypereosinophilic syndrome.
Vasculitis is typically absent histologically with negative direct immunofluorescence.

questions.stem: Which of the following drugs is most likely to cause drug-induced subacute lupus erythematosus?
questions.explanation:
Thiazidc diuretics are the commonest drugs that may cause drug-induced subacute r.utaneous lupus -?.rythematosus followed by terbinafine, calcium channel blockers and ACE inhibitors.
Frusemide is associated with the development of bullous pemphigoid and photosensitivity but not with subacute cutaneous lupus erythematosus.
Anti-histone antibodies are positive in around 50% of the cases of drug-induced sub acute cutaneous lupus erythematosus as opposed to around 80% in drug-induced systemic lupus erythematosus.

questions.stem: Sebaceous glands can be found in which cyst walls of the following?
options: Epidermoid cysts & eruptive vellus hair cysts.
questions.explanation:
Sebaceous cysts are found in steatocystoma multiplex and are absent in the other forms of cysts.
Both epidermoid and eruptive vellus hair cysts are composed of epidermal lining.
However, in the latter vellus hair can be found in the contents of the cysts.
Pilar cysts are composed of the outer hair root sheath lining, which is characterised by absence of the granular layer.

questions.stem: A 22-year-old man presented with multiple palpable purpura and petechiae on his buttocks and legs three weeks following a sore throat. He also had symptoms of abdominal pain and ankle swelling. In this condition, which of the following statementsis correct?
options: Direct immunofluorescence will show deposition of both IgM and IgG peri-vascularly.
Direct immunofluorescence will show IgA deposition peri-vascularly.
Pulmonary haemorrhage is the commonest co-morbidity In this condition
Renal involvement is extremely uncommon and its presence is often transient.
The condition is associated with a higher mortality rate in children compared to adults.
questions.explanation:
Henoch-Schonlein purpura is an immune-mediated small vessel vasculitis characterised by deposition of IgA complexes in the small blood vessels.
It may affect the skin and kidney.
The conditon may be recurrent with both skin and renal involvement hence monitor Ing for up to six months is recommended even in the absence of any positive urinalysis on the initial investigation.
The disease in adults has a higher morbidity with the potential for chronic renal in volvement compared to children.
The commonest organs affected in this condition are the small Joints, kidney, skin and gut wall.

questions.stem: In which of the following conditions is monoclonal gammopathy usually not found?
questions.explanation:
Scleromyxoedema is most likely to be associated with IgG monoclonal gammopathy although other variants may also be possible.
Schnitzler's syndrome is most likely to be associated with IgM monoclonal gammopathy.
Erythema elevatum diutinum is most likely to be associated with IgA monoclonal gammopathy.
Necrobiotic xanthogranuloma can be associated with any sub-type of monoclonal gammopathy.
other conditions that may be associated with monoclonal gammopathies include cryogobulinaemia types 1 and 2, Sweet's syndrome and pyoderma gangrenosum.

questions.stem: Which of the following choices is the major criterion for the diagnosis of systemic mastocytosis?
options: Positivity to CD2/C:D25 on mast cells.
Presence of 25% or more mast cells with atypical or spindle-shaped appearance.
Presence of large mast cell infiltrate in the bone marrow, spleen or liver.
questions.explanation:
In order to diagnose systemic mastocytosis one major criterion is required together with the presence of one minor criterion.
All the other choices are minor criteria for the diagnosis of mastocytosis.
The presence of raised serum tryptase levels in cases of cutaneous mastocytosis may indicate the presence of systemic involvement and may therefore necessitate further investigations.
Osteoporosis can occur in cases of systemic mastocytosis.
Patients with systemic mastocytosis are at increased risk of developing anaphylaxis and should avoid drugs that can potentially trigger the mast cells.

questions.stem: In which of the following drug-induced reactions is facial oedema a common manifestation?
options: Drug reaction with eosinophillia and systemic symptoms.
questions.explanation:
In acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis small monomorphic pustules may appear on the face however facial oedema often occurs in the setting of drug reaction with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms.
Serum-sickness-like reaction presents with fever, arthralgia and urticaria due to a drug, although unlike serum-slcirness reaction, vasculitis is not a feature and the complement levels are within normal range.
Stevens-Johnson's syndrome affetis the mucosal sites but facial oedema is not a feature of the condition.

questions.stem: Which of the following is not a proposed pathogenic mechanism for acnevulgaris?
options: Presence and activity of propionibacterium acne.

questions.stem: Which of the following chromosomal aberrations is associated with severe acne?
questions.explanation: The severe form of acne 'Acne conglobata' has been reported to be more common and more severe in XYY chromosomal aberration than in normal subjects.

questions.stem: A 35-year-old man presented with a 6-month history of mouth ulcers and painful blistering eruption on the trunk accompanied by painful warty growths over the groin and axillae. Widespread erythematous and annular plaques with flaccid blisters on trunk and limbs are present along with exophytic plaques on the axillae, groins and peri-anal skin. Extensive erosions are present on the buccal mucosa and papillomatous vegetating lesions on the angles of the mouth. Skin biopsy shows intra-epidermal neutrophilic microabscesses. Direct immunofluorescence shows epidermal intercellular IgG staining and linear and granular C3 at the dermal-epidermal junction. Indirect immunofluoresence on rat bladder epithelium is negative. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation:
Pemphigus vegetans (PV) is the rarest variant of pemphlgus accounting for 2%- 5.7% of cases.
Flaccid bullae or pustules and hypertrophic papillated plaques involve the face, skin folds and oral mucosa.
Vegetative and hypertrophic lesions arise from eroded pustules and bullae.
The two clinical subclasses of PV; Hallopeau and Neumann type have similar histological and immunofluoresence features.
Neumann type follows more aggressive course and its treatment can be challenging.
Oral corticosteroids, dapsone, azathioprine, retinoids, etanercept and extra corporeal photopheresis have been used.

questions.stem: Which of the following is associated with flagellate hyperpigmentation?
questions.explanation:
Certain drugs may produce a specific pattern of hyperpigmentation.
Flagellate hyperpigmentation-bleomycin or zidovudine.
Diffuse hyperpigmentation on the pcllms and soles - cyclophosphamide or doxorubicin.
Localized hyperpigmentation around small joints - bleomycin and doxorubicin.
Melasma-like pigmentation-oestrogen-related hormonal substances and phenytoin-like medications.
Nail unit involvement - zidovudine, psoralens, minocycline, antimalarials and Gold.
Mucosal hyperpigmentation - cyclophosphamide, doxorubicin, zidovudine, minocycline and some heavy metals.
Blue-grey pigmentation in sun-exposed areas - amiodarone.
Yellow-brown to bluish-gray pigmentation on the face, the neck, the lower extremities, and the forearms - hydroxychloroquine.
Exogenous ochronosis - chronic hydroquinone use.
Bluish-gray pigmentation, especially in sun-exposed areas, and pigmentations of the conjunctivae - chlorpromazine and related phenothiazines.
Skin, nails, scleral and oral mucosal, thyroid, bones, and teeth hyperpigmentation - mino:::ycline.

questions.stem: A 40-year-old man complains of recurrent burning eruption on the glans penis. Examiniltion shows hyperpigmentation over the glans penis. He has had recurrent episodes over the past 2 years. Which of the following is most likely to be implicated?
questions.explanation:
This patient describes symptoms of a fixed drug eruption (FOE).
FOE recurs at the same site with each administration of the drug.
Most common sites for FOE include face and genitalia, but can occur anywhere.
Localised erythema leading to blistering is commonly seen.
Blistering may not always be present.
Hyperpigmentation occurs following resolution of the erythema and blistering.
Most commonly implicated medications include phenolphthalein in laxatives, sulphonamides, beta-lactams antibiotics, tetracyclines,barbiturates, gold, oral contraceptives and aspirin.

questions.stem: A 60-year-old man was admitted to ICU with sepsis. A few days later he developed pruritus and erythema over the upper trunk associated with angioedema. Which is the most likely cause of his symptoms?
questions.explanation:
Pruritus, erythema and angioedema over the upper body are associated with intravenous administration of vancomycin-the so-called red man syndrome.
It is thought to be secondary to histamine release and can be prevented by administering antihistamines. Rifampicin has been reported to cause similar reactions.

questions.stem: Which of the following is not true of Grover's disease?
options: A history of sun-exposure is often forthcoming.
ATP2A2 mutations similar to Darier's disease have been identified.
Can resemble Darier's disease on histology.
Features of Hailey-Hailey disease may be seen on histology.
The rash can be persistent in some patients.
questions.explanation:
Grover's disease (transient acantholytic dermatosis) presents as pruritic, papulovesicular eruption on the trunk.
Seen in adults with a history of chronic sun damage.
Histological examination shows variable focal aciantholytic dyskeratosis resembling, Darier's disease, Hailey-Hailey disease or pemphigus.
Classic (transient) form resolves within a few months, but a persistent form has been recognized.
Unlike Darier's disease there is no evidence for genetic predisposition.

questions.stem: Which of the following types of porokeratoses is not associated with malignant epithelial neoplasm?
questions.explanation:
Malignant epithelial neoplasms are reported in all sub-types except the punctate variety.
The risk is the highest with linear porokeratosis and giant porokeratosis of Mibelli.

questions.stem: Fogo selvagem is a subtype of which of the following?
questions.explanation:
Fogo selvagem is an endemic form of pemphigus foliaceus.
It is endemic in rural Brazil and it means "wild fire" in Portuguese.
It is clinically, histologically, and immunopathologically similar to sporadic pemphigus foliaceus.
The geographic distribution of disease clustering is similar to that of a black fly, Simulium nigrimanum.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements isincorrect?
options: Guineapig oesophagus is more sensitive for detecting pemphigus foliaceous antibodies.
igGstaining is present on the cell surface of epidermal cells in pemphigus vulgaris.
Monkey oesophagus is more sensitive for detecting pemphigus vulgaris anti bodies.
Pemphigus vulgaris and foliaceous display similar direct immunofluorescence findings.
There is no correlation between the titre of circulating anti-cell surface anti body and disease activity in pemphigus vulgaris and foliaceous.
questions.explanation:
It is usually not possible to differentiate between pemphigus vulgaris and foliaceous on immunofluoresence findings as it is similar in both disorders.
IgG staining is present on the cell surface of epidermal cells throughout the epidermis in both disorders.
In general, monkey oesophagus is more sensitive for detecting pemphigus vulgaris antibodies.
Guniea pig oesophagus is a superior substrate for detecting pemphigus foliaceous antibodies.
There is a positive, correlation between the titre of circulating anti-cell surface an tibodv and the disease activity in pemphigus vulgaris and foliaceous. However, this correlation is not perfect (unlike in bullous pemphigoid where there is no correlation between the antibodies and disease activity).
Disease activity in individual patient does not necessarily correlate with antibody titre; therefore, clinical findings should not be replaced by immunofluoresence titres in monitoring the disease.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is true regarding drug-induced pemphigus?
options: Patients do not exhibit auto-antibodies to desmoglein 1 and desmoglein 3.
Pemphigus foliaceous is the commonest morphological pattern.
Remission after drug withdrawal is uncommon.
questions.explanation:
The prevalence of pemphigus in penicillamine users is estimated to be approximately 7 percent.
Pemphigus foliaceous is more common than pemphigus vulgaris in these patients.
Direct and indirect immunofluorescence are positive.
Auto-antibodies to sporadic pemphigus antigens desmoglein 1 and desmoglein 3 have been noted.
Most patients go into remission after stopping the offending drug.
ACE inhibitors have been implicated in both pemphigus vulgaris and foliaceous.

questions.stem: A 45-year-old woman presents with a few months history of diffuse hair loss. She complains of losing a lot of hair whilst combing. Her past medical history includes breast cancer for which she has recently received chemotherapy. Examination shows diffuse non-scarring alopecia. What is the likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation:
Anagen effluvium is usually seen after cancer chemotherapy.
Telogen effluvium can also result from cancer chemotherapy or stress.
Anagen effluvium results from inhibition or arrest of cell division in the hair matrix which leads to narrow weakened segment of the hair shaft that is susceptible to fracture with minimal trauma.
The characteristic finding in anagen effluvium is the tapered fracture of the hair shafts as a result of damage to the matrix.
.. Anagen and telogen effluvium can be differentiatedon pull test, where more anagen hair will be seen.
Pull test is negative in diffuse alopecia areata.
Exclamation hair mark hairs can be seen in alopecia areata.

questions.stem: A 34-year-old lady presented with a long-standing painful ulcer on the lateral aspect of the right lower leg which has been presen'i for 6 months and did not respond to various dressings and compression bandages. On examination, there was evidence of livecio reticularis on the lower legs and the patient gives a history of a previouspulmonary embolism and two spontaneous miscarriages. Laboratory examination showed mild thrombocytosis. The most likely diagnosis here is:
questions.explanation:
Painful chronic ulcers in young people can be secondary to vasculitis, and in thiscase, the presence of livedo reticularis, history of pulmonary embolism and miscarriages is highly suggestive of anti-phospholipid syndrome.
Investigations should include a full vasculitis screen and auto-antibodies which include anti-cardiolipin and anti-phospholipid antibodies.
Treatment with aspirin should be commenced.
This condition can co-exist with systemic lupus erythematosus.
Cryoglobulinaemia can present with livedo reticularis and vasculitic lesions. These tend to be acral and exacerbated on exposure to cold temperatures. Although this would still be a possibility in this patient,.;nti-phospholipid syndrome is more likely due to the history of miscarriages and pulmonary emboli.
Henoch-Schonlein purpura is a form of vasculitis where immune complexes withpre dominantly IgA antibodies occur in the buttocks and legs, and may be associated with throat, abdominal pain, arthralgia and renal involvement.
Around 1% of patients may progress to develop end stage renal failure.

questions.stem: A 28-year-old man who has been on penicillamine for several years presented with an asymptomatic annular eruption on the right side of the neck which consists of keratotic papules. There is no associated scaling or erythema. The most likely diagnosis is:
questions.explanation:
Elastosis perforans serpiginosa is a disorder in which there is trans-epidermal illumination of elastic fibres.
Although the condition may occur spontaneously, this can also occur secondarv to penicillamine or in patients with Marfan's or Ehler's-Danlos syndrome.
The clinical description does not tit with the other diagnoses mentioned (e.g. granuloma annulare does not have a keratotic surface).

questions.stem: A 37-year-old lady was referred to the dermatology department with a 3-year history of urticarial lesions that failed to respond to various anti-histamines given by her GP. Further history reveals that the individual wheals persist for days before they disappear. This often leaves post-inflammatory pigmentation. There is also associated bone pain and an associated paraproteinaemia. The most likely diagnosis here is:
questions.explanation:
Schnitzler's syndrome is a rare disorder which is characterised by the presence of urticariaI-like lesions that often persist for days or even weeks, and is associated with bone pain and paraproteinaemia.
Bone pain can often be severe.
Muckle-Wells syndrome can present with limb pain and an urticarial-like eruption, however, this is often associated with recurrent fever, amyloidosis and deafness. This is an autosomal dominant disorder due to CIASl defect.
Although urticarial vasculitis can present with urticarial lesions that persist for days leaving post inflammatory hyperpigmentation, this is often associated with arthralgia, rather than bone pain.

questions.stem: A 34-year-old lady has been troubled with persistent acne over the last 10 years with hirsutism, hair loss and menstrual irregularities. Polycystic ovarian syndrome has bP.en excluded by various hormonal testing and imaging by the gynaecologist.She is on a number of medications, one of which could be the cause of her symptoms. Which of the following medications is most likely to be associated with these symptoms?
questions.explanation:
Sodium valproate is an anti-epileptic and can rarely produce an acneiform eruption together with a clinical and biochemical picture that is similar to polycystic ovarian syndrome.
Lithium and prednisolone can both cause acneiform eruptions, however, this if often monomorphic in nature and would not explain the signs of hyperandrogenism.
Minocycline can be used in acne; the possible side effects are a lupus-like syndrome, hepatitis and pigmentation.

questions.stem: A 26-year-old lady with a history of photosensitivity developed an annular erythematous rash with scaling, predominantly on her shoulders and upper chest following exposure to sunlight. Her laboratory investigations showed a strong positivity to the anti-Ro antibody. She wishes to become pregnant in the near future and has asked whether the foetus can come to any harm. Which of the following statement is true?
options: There is a small risk of congenital heart block of the foetus.
There is risk of cleft lip to the foetus.
This condition and laboratory findings have no effect on the pregnancy.
questions.explanation:
Subacute lupus erythematosus and a positive Ro antibody indicate a strong degree of photosensitivity and the risk of developing a congenital heart block in the foetus.
Close collaboration with the obstetricians is required.
There is also a risk of neonatal lupus erythematosus; however, this is often transient and will disappear within the first few months of life due to the passive transfer of IgG antibodies.

questions.stem: You demonstrate to a group of medical students that detachment of the epidermis can occur with gentle lateral pressure in certain dermatological conditions. This sign is positive in which of the following conditions?
questions.explanation:
The Nikolsky's sign is positive when gentle lateral pressure on the skin leads to shear ing/detachment of the epidermal component.
Second degree burns can also exhibit the Nikolsky's sign.

questions.stem: A patient is referred to you for assessment of bluish discolouration of his proximal fingernails. Blue lanulae" of the nails can occur with which of the following?
questions.explanation:
Mepacrine use can also give a blue-grey discolouration of the hard palate.
Potassium permanganate soaks can give rise to brown nails.
Tetracycline can cause photo-onycholysls which may be the sole manifestation of phototoxicity.
Pseuclomonasaeruglnosa infection can give rise to green discolouration of the nails.
Oal'ier's disease may have longitudinal erythro-and/or leukonychia.

questions.stem: Which of the following does not exhibit antibodies to BPAG2 or its metabolic products?
questions.explanation:
Antibodies against BPAG2 or its metabolic products are seen in patients with bullous pemphigoid, pemphigoid gestationis, linear IgA disease, cicatricial pemphigoid, and lichen planus pemphigoides.
The clinical appear nce, immunofluoresence and type of infiltrate can help differentiate between these conditions (e.g. neutrophilic infiltrate in linear IgA as opposed to eosinophilic in bullous pemphigoid).

questions.stem: Which of the following statements regarding myasthenia gravis, thymoma and pemphigus is false?
options: Irradiation of thymus or thymectomy may not improve the pemphigus dis ease activity.
Myasthenia gravis and thymoma are associated with pemphigus vulgaris and pemphigus foliaceous.
The course of myasthenia gravis follows the course of pemphigus.
Thymic abnormality may either precede or follow the onset of pemphigus.
Thymoma may be associated with paraneoplastic pemphigus.
questions.explanation:
Myasthenia gravis, thymoma, or both have been associated with pemphigus vulgaris and pemphigus foliaceous.
Thymoma may be associated with PV and PF and with paraneoplastic pemphigus.
The course of myasthenia gravis is independent of pemphigus.
Thymic abnormality may either precede or follow the onset of pemphigus.
Irradiation of thymus or thymectomy may not improve pemphigus disease activity.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements regarding paraneoplastic pemphigus is false?
options: Blistering, lichenoid, or erythema multiforme-like lesions may be seen.
High fatality from disease complications, including pulmonary involvement with respiratory failure.
Most common underlying malignancy is thymoma.
questions.explanation:
Paraneoplastic pemphigus is a rare complication of malignancies of which non- Hodgkin lymphoma or chronic lymphocytic leukaemia are the commonest.
Painful, erosive stomatitis is commonly seen.
Polymorphous cutaneous lesions includingblisters and erosionsmay be seen in addition to morbilliform, or lichenoid lesions.
Anti-plakin antibodies are detected by indirect immunofluorescence against rodent bladder epithelium.
There is high fatality from disease complications, Including sepsis, pulmonary in volvement with respiratory failure or bronchiolitisobliterans.

questions.stem: Which of the following is associated with increased risk of internal malignancy?
questions.explanation:
The relative risk for cancer increases with anti-epiligrin cicatricial pemphigoid.
The time between blister onset and cancer diagnosis is approximately 14 months.
The risk for cancer appears higher in the first year of disease.
Relative risk for malignancy with anti-epillgrin cicatricial pemphigoid approximates that for adults with dermatomyositis.

questions.stem: Which of the following is not a feature of Brunsting-Perry pemphigoid?
options: Head and neck involvement is common.
questions.explanation:
Brunsting-Perry pemphigoid is a locally recurrent and scarring sub-epidermal blistering disorder.
Head or neck involvement is common.
Patients are typically elderly.
Brunsting-Perry pemphigoid predominates in elderly men.
Mucous membrane involvement is uncommon.

questions.stem: Which of the following is not true regarding pemphigoid gestationis?
options: Direct immunofluorescence shows linear deposition of immunoglobulinG without C3.
Newborns may be affected with bullous lesions.
Usually occurs in the second-third trimester.
questions.explanation:
Pemphigoid gestationis (PG) is a pruritic, vesiculobullous eruption of acute-onset.
Seen in the second-third trimester or the immediate postpartum period.
Flares may occur around delivery.
Shows a strong association with HLA-DR3, -DR4, and a C4 null allele.
First onset usually on the abdomen and umbilicus.
Spares the face, mucous membranes, palms, and soles.
Newborns may be affected.
Histopathology shows dermo-epidermal separation with numerous eosinophils.
Direct immunofluorescence shows linear deposition of C3 (almost 100%), with or without immunoglobulin G.
Indirect IF only occasionally detects circulating IgG deposition.
Sera from most PG patients react to a 180-kd transmembrane protein with a collagenous domain.
No significant maternal morbidity or mortality.
Associated with a slight increase in premature and small-for-gestational-age births.

questions.stem: Which of the following is true regarding the prognosis of Pemphigoid gestationis?
options: May flare in the post-partum period.
Recurrences are rare with oral contraceptive and menstruation.
questions.explanation:
Pemphigoid gestationis has a variable clinical presentation and course.
Spontaneous resolution during the latter part of gestation is common but dramatic post-partum flares may be seen.
Recurrences with menstruation and flares with use of oral contraceptives occur in at least 25%.
Spontaneous disease regression may occur during the third trimester but the disease may flare during parturition.

questions.stem: Which of the following systemic diseases is most commonly associated with epidermolysis bullosa acquisita?
questions.explanation:
Epidermolysis bullosa acquisita may be associated with various autoimmune systemic diseases:
Inflammatory bowel disease (commonest).
Systemic lupus erythematosus.
Amyloidosis.
Thyroiditis.
Multiple endocrinopathy syndrome.
Rheumatoid arthritis.
Pulmonary fibrosis.
Chronic lymphocytic leukemia.
rhymoma.
Diabetes mellitus.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is false?
options: ELISA can differentiate pemphigus vulgaris from pemphigusfoliaceous.
ELISA is more sensitive than indirect immunofluoresence for pemphigus vulgaris and pemphigus folicaeous.
ELISA ispositive for both desmogleins 3 and 1 in pemphigus vulgaris.
ELISA ispositive for desmoglein 1 in mucosal pemphigus vulgaris.
ELISA is positive for only desmoglein 1 in pemphigus foliaceous.
questions.explanation:
Enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) is more sensitive and specific than immunofluorescence in differentiating pemphigus vulgaris from pemphigus foliaceous.
ELISA titer correlates better than that of indirect immunofluorescence with disease activity.
ELISA is positive for desmoglein 3 (but not desmoglein 1) in mucosal pemphigus vulgaris.
ELISA is positive for both desmogleins 3 and 1 in pemphigus vulgaris with both mucosal and skin involvement.
ELISA is positive for only desmoglein 1 in PF.

questions.stem: A 48-year-old alcoholic man was admitted with ascites and decompensated liver failure. He was noted to have a purpuric, perifollicular eruption on his legs. Significant bruising was also noted on his abdomen. What investigation would you request to make the diagnosis?
options: Urine dip stick for protein and blood.
questions.explanation:
Scurvy is characterized by general weakness, anaemia, gingivitis and petichieae.
It is caused by a prolonged deficiency of vitamin C (ascorbic acid) in the diet.
Vitamin C plays a crucial role in the formation of collagen.
It isuncommon in modern society but can still be encountered in high risk population which includes institutionalised patients and alcoholics.
Skin signs of scurvy include perifollicular hyperkeratotic papules, often on the shins.
These appear as reddish/bluish bruise-like spots surrounding hair follicles. The central hairs are twisted like corkscrews that may break easily.
The papules may join together to form large areas of palpable purpura or ecchymoses.
Diagnosis is based on clinical findings.
Plasma ascorbic acid level may help in establishing the diagnosis, but this level tends to reflect the recent dietary intake rather than the actual tissue levels of vitamin C.
Signs of scurvy can occur with low-normal serum levels of vitamin C.
The level of vitamin C in leukocytes more accurately correlates to tissue stores com pared with serum levels because these cells are not affected acutely by circadian rhythm or dietary changes.
Confirmation of the diagnosis can be achieved by resolution following vitamin Cad ministration.

questions.stem: A 7O-year old woman is admitted with tense blisters developing on a background of eczematous skin. A skin biopsy is performed for histology and immunofluoresence. Histology confirms your diagnosis of bullous pemphigoid. Which of the following statements is true of immunofluoresence in bullous pemphigoid?
options: Approximately 50% of patients have circulating anti-basement membrane zone IgG.
Bullous pemphigoid IgG causes complement activation by the alternate pathway.
C3 may be the sole immunoreactant on direct immunofluorescence of peri-lesional skin.
Indirect immunofluorescence antibody titer correlates with disease activity.
On lM NaCl induced blister, bullous pemphigoid antibodies bind to the floor of the blister.
questions.explanation:
In pemphigoid, direct immunofluorescence of peri-lesional skin reveals linear deposition of IgG and C3 at the epidermal basement membrane.
Although both C3 and IgG are detected in most patients, C3 may be the sole immunoreactant.
Approximately 70 - 80 % of patients with bullous pemphigoid have circulating anti basement membrane zone IgG.
On artificially splitting the skin with lM NaCl, bullous pemphigoid antibodies bind to the roof of the blister while epidermolysis bullosa acquisita antibodies bind to the floor of the blister.
In bullous pemphigoid, the indirect immunofluorescence antibody titer does not usually correlate with disease extent or activity.
Bullous pemphigoid IgG causes complement activation by the classic pathway, with activation of the alternative pathway by the C3 amplification mechanism.

questions.stem: A 40-year-old man presented with a 6-months history of an intensely pruritic eruption which started on his limbs and genitalia. Close examination shows shiny polygonal papules with a violaceus colour; all papules were flat-topped. Examination of the mouth shows a reticular white appearance on both buccal mucosae. The diagnosis here is:
questions.explanation:
The appearance of pruritic, polygonal, purple and plane papules (SPs) Is characteristic of lichen planus.
Oral and genital examination should always be performed when the diagnosis is suspected.
Erosive lichen planus can cause scarring.
Other variants of lichen planus include: hypertrophic, atrophic, drug-induced, lichen planus pemphigoides and lichen planus pigmentosa.

questions.stem: A 20-year-old patient presents with depigmented patches on the trunk and limbs. There are no associated symptoms. Which auto-immune condition is most likely to be associated with this condition?
questions.explanation:
Many auto-immune disorders can be associated with vitiligo but thyroid disease is the commonest.
Measurement of thyroid antibodies should be considered in patients with vitiligo as a high titre - even in the presence of normal thyroid function tests indicates the risk for future thyroid disease.

questions.stem: A 32-year-old female presented with a 4-week history of a mildly burning rash on the upper arms and torso. Examination showed erythematous annular and polycyclic plaques with scaling without scarring. She has marked photosensitivity. The presence of which antibod,yn this condition may be associated with a congenital heart block in the foetus?
questions.explanation:
The diagnosis is sub-acute lupus erythematosus (LE) which can present in an annular or psoriasiform pattern.
Sub-acute LE can be drug induced with thiazides being the commonest implicated.
Unlike discoid LE, this variant is not associated with scarring.
Anti-Ro antibodies are associated with marked photosensitivity and the risk of developing congenital cardiac defects in the foetus.

questions.stem: A 60-year-old man presented with a 3-month history of an eruption that consisted of flaccid pustules in the trunk and groin with background erythema. Close examination showed flaccid bullae and pustules containing a fluid level giving the appearance of a hypopyon. Some pustules and bullae had ruptured forming an annular pattern of scaling. The patient had a background of IgAparaprotinaemia. What is the first-line systemic treatment for this condition in the absence of any contra-indications?
questions.explanation:
The diagnosis here is subcorneal pustular dermatosis, also called Sneddon Wilkinson disease.
The condition can be associated with myeloma or a paraprotinaemla and these should always be investigated once the diagnosis has been made.
Although all the above treatments have been used, dapsone remains the most effective treatment for subcorneal pustular dermatosis.
Dapsone is also very effective for dermatitis herpetiformis and bullous lupus erythematosus.
