Naevus sebaceous represents a congenital hamartoma of sebaceous elements most commonly found on the scalp.
Although it is present at birth, it acquires a verrucous appearance at puberty.
Other lesions that may arise from it include basal cell carcinoma and trichoblastoma.

questions.stem: A 23-year-old woman presented with a 1 cm firm nodule on the lower leg which has been present for 8 months. She is unsure as to how thisappeared. Examination showed a firm flesh-coloured nodule with no surface change which puckered on gentle squeezing of the edges. The most likely diagnosis is:
questions.explanation:
The description is of a dermatofibroma which is a histiocytic lesion that often occurs on the lower legs of women and may be related to an insect bite or trauma.
Nodular melanoma should always be included in the differential of a nodule on the leg as it can be amelanotic.
The firm consistency and puckering on squeezing should aid in the diagnosis of a dermatofibroma.

questions.stem: Which of the following treatments is the least suitable treatment for superficial basal cell carcinoma?
questions.explanation:
Diclofenac sodium (Solaraze) gel is only licensed for the treatment of thin actinic keratoses.
Although all other treatments listed can be used, the choice will depend on the site, size, thickness and overall risk of recurrence.

questions.stem: In which anatomical sites do squamous cell carcinomas have worst prognosis?
questions.explanation:
The prognosis and risk of metastasis of squamous cell carcinoma depend on several factors which include size, histology (poorly-differentiated) and past medical history (transplant patients are at particular risk).
Squamous cell carcinoma arising on the ear is associated with a poor prognosis.

questions.stem: Which of the following is not a poor prognostic factor in cutaneou5 squamous cell carcinoma (SCC)?
questions.explanation:
Factors determining poor prognosis in cutaneous SCC include tumour size > 2 cm, tumour depth) 2 mm (especially 6 mm), tumour at sites of radiation, thermal damage, ulceration, sinuses, inflammation, scars or Bowen's disease, non-exposed sites, ear, and lip.
Spindle cell (carcinosarcomas), acantholytic, desmoplastic histological subsets.
Histological features of aggression including perineural or perivascuiar involvement, or both, Broders' grades 3 and 4, host immunosuppression and recurrent lesions, lymph-node involvement or distant metastasis.

questions.stem: A 70-year-old man presents with a biopsy-proven basal cell carcinoma (BCC) on his forehead. He had this lesion treated with radiotherapy nearly 4 years ago. Which of the following is contra-indicated for the treatment of this lesion?
questions.explanation:
Side-effects of radiotherapy include dyspigmentation, telangiectasia, and radiodys trophy, resulting in a poor cosmetic outcome.
Radiotherapy is contra-indicated In the treatment of BCCs that have recurred after radiotherapy.

questions.stem: A 68-year-old patient has superficial basal cell carcinomas(sBCCs) on the upper chest. The dermatologist has prescribed a cream which acts by stimulating toll-like receptor 7. The active ingredient in the cream is:
questions.explanation:
imiquimod is a synthetic immune-response modifier belonging to the imidazoqulnolone family.
It acts by stimulating toll-like receptor 7, which is expressed on dendritic cells and monocytes, leading to increased production of cytokines and chemokines, which in turn promote both T-helper-1 innate and adaptive cell-mediated immune responses.
Topical 5% imiquimod cream is an emerging non-invasive therapeutic option for sBCCs.
Local skin reactions including erythema, oedema, pruritus, erosion, ulceration, dyspigmentation,and scabbing are common side-effects.

questions.stem: Whilst reading a histopathology report you come across the term Breslow thickness. You are aware that this determines the prognosis in cutaneous melanoma. Breslow thickness is measured from:
questions.explanation:
Breslow tumour thickness is measured from the top of the granular layer or the base of an ulcer to the deepest point of tumour invasion using an optical micrometer.
As a general rule the thicker the Breslow thickness, the poorer the prognosis.

questions.stem: A 58-year-old man underwent excision of a yellow nodule on the upper eyelid that is histologically confirmed as sebaceous adenoma. He has a family history of colonic carcinoma. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation:
Muir-Torre syndrome refers to the presence of sebaceous adenoma, sebaceoma, or sebaceous carcinoma with visceral cancer, usually gastrointestinal or genito-urinary.
Patients may also present with other cutaneous lesions including keratoacanthoma, squamous cell carcinoma, or multiple follicular cysts.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the most important prognostic factor in the diagnosis of melanoma?
questions.explanation:
The thickness, measured as Breslow thickness, is the most important prognostic factor in melanoma.
All other factors are also important but the surviv2I rate strongly correlates with the thickness of the tumour.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the most common site for sebaceous carcinoma?
questions.explanation:
Sebaceous carcinoma is a rare malignancy that typically affects the eyelids.
Around 25% of the cases can be extra-ocular.
Sebaceous carcinoma is the fourth most common eyelid malignancy after basal cell carcinoma, squamous cell carcinoma and melanoma.
Sebaceous carcinomas can metastasise and these tumours should be treated adequately through surgical excision.
The presence of sebaceous carcinoma (in addition to sebaceoma and/or sebaceous adenoma) raises a suspicion of the presence of Muir-Torre syndrome.

questions.stem: All of the following conditions can increase the risk of developing basal cell carcinomas in children except:
questions.explanation:
There is an increased risk for the development of melanoma arising from giant con genital naevi and not basal cell carcinomas.
All other conditions have an increased risk of developing basal cell carcinomas.
The commonest benign tumour which arises from the naevus sebaceous is syringocystoadenomapapilliferum.
Patients with Gorlin's syndrome are known to develop multiple basal cell carcinomas from an early age.
Patients with xeroderma pigmentosum are at increased risk of developing skin cancers including squamous cell carcinoma and melanoma.

questions.stem: Which of the following markers is a sensitive marker for Merkel cell carcinoma?
questions.explanation:
Merkel cell carcinoma is a rare neuro-endocrine cutaneous malignancy that may arise in transplant patients.
Recently a virus has been implicated as a possible factor in the development of Merkel cell carcinoma called polyoma virus.
CK20 is a very sensitive marker for Merkel cell carcinoma.
CD34 and Factor XIIIa are helpful to distinguish between dermatofibroma and dematofibrosarcoma protuberans.
CD1a and S100 are helpful to differentiate between Langerhan's cells and melanocytes.

questions.stem: A 36-year-old man has had a changing mole on his back removed. This was reported histologically to be a superficial spreading melanoma, Breslow thickness of 3.4 mm with no ulceration.Sentinel node biopsy did not show any evidence of positive lymph nodes and there were no systemic features to suggest distant metastases. The pathological staging of this tumour is:
questions.explanation:
Stage Ila is Breslow thickness 1.01-2 mm with ulceration or a Breslow thickness be tween 2.01-4 mm without ulceration in the absence of clinical, radiographic or histological evidence of lymph node involvement.
Stage lb is Breslow thick,,ess less than 1 mm but with ulceration or mitoses equal to or more than 1 per mm2.
Stage IV is presence of distant metastases.

questions.stem: A 50-year-old man presented with non-tender papules and nodules with no surface changes on the back. He had recently been complaining of night sweats and weight loss. Histology of the lesion showed a dense dermal infiltrate which stained negative for CD3, CD20, CD79a, bcl-2, bcl-6, CD4, CD30 and CDS and was positive for CD43 and myeloperoxidase. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation:
The negative staining to the T-cell markers CD3, CD4 and CDSrules out mycosis fungoides.
The negative staining to the B-cell markers CD20 and CD79a rules out cutaneous 8 cell lymphomas.
CD43 positivity is a clue for myeloid leukaemia (leukaemia cutis in this case) in the absence of positivity to Band T cell markers.
Myeloid leukaemia also stains positive to myeloperoxidase.

questions.stem: You remove a suspicious mole on the shoulder of a young woman who had excessive sun exposure. The result showed a superficial spreading melanoma with a Breslow thickness of 0.7 mm with no mitoses or ulceration. You arrange for urgent action but the patient informs you that she is now 8 weeks pregnant. Which of the followihg actions should take place?
options: Defer any further intervention until after delivery of the baby.
Wide local excision with 1 cm margin.
Wide local excision with 2 cm margin.
questions.explanation:
Whilst It is good practice to defer most non-urgent and benign lesions removal till after delivery, pregnancy should not be a contra-indication for a wide local excision of a melanoma.
Melanoma is not very radiosensitive however adjunctive radiotherapy may be i.;sed post positive sentinel lymph node lymphadenectomy particularly if th II? was extra-capsular spread of the tumour or more than 3 lymph nodes were involved.

questions.stem: You see a 61-year-old Australian man with a 3 cm ulcerated nodule below his left eye that has been growing over the last 5 months. On further examination the nodule appears tethered and attached the underlying:,tructures. A biopsy performed a week earlier showed a poorly-differentiated squamous cell carcinoma. What should be the next action?
options: Surgical excision with a margin of 1 cm.
Surgical excision with amargin of 6 mm.
questions.explanation: In cases of skin tumours which are large and/or tethered and attached to underlying structures imaging should be arranged to assess for local invasion.

questions.stem: You are looking after a patient with cutaneous T-cell lymphoma. At what stage of their disease would you consider introducing Bexarotene?
questions.explanation:
Bexarotene is a retinoid receptor agonist.
It is often combined,..,.ith other therapies such as PUVA or extrariorporeal photopheresis.
Side effects include hypothyroidism and dyslipidaemia, requiring regular monitoring of thyroid function and lipids.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements regarding Vismodegib is true?
options: It inhibits the hedgehog receptor and Its most common side effect is muscle cramps.
It inhibits the smoothened receptor and its most common side effect is nausea.
It inhibits the smoothened receptor and its most common side effect is muscle cramps.
It inhibits the hedgehog receptor and its most common side effect is nausea.
questions.explanation:
Vismodegib inhibits the smoothened receptor, a key mediator in the Hedgehog signalling pathway.
Other commonly-seen side-effects include altered taste sensation anorexia, diarrhoea, fatigue and alopecia.

questions.stem: Which HPV serotype is most commonly associated with subungual squamous cell carcinoma?
questions.explanation:
Periungual skin is the most common extr2-genital site for cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma.
Subungal squamous cell carcinoma is commonly a diagnostic challenge, presenting with a variety of nail changes including verruciform hyperkeratosis, dystrophy, longitudinal ridging, onycholysis, erythronychia, subungal haematomas and paronychia.
Whilst all subtypes listed are high-risk for subungal squamous cell carcinoma, the most important carcinogenic factor is HPV 16.
Longitudinal nail biopsy is the gold standard diagnostic approach as this allows sampling of the nail bed. matrix and fold.

questions.stem: What is the second most common site for melanoma in British Caucasian men?
questions.explanation:
As reported by the Statistical Information Team at Cancer Research UK, the commonest site for melanoma in men is the trunk (accounting for 41% of cases), followed by the head and neck (22%) and arms (19%).
For women, the commonest s;te is the legs (39%), followed by the arms (24%) and trunk (20%).

questions.stem: A 14-year-old boy with red hair and freckled skin is referred by hisGP due to concern regarding a number of atypical moles. On taking a family history you establishthat his father, older sister and paternal uncle, all of a similar complexion, had malignant melanoma before the age of 40. Mutation in which gene is most likely to underlie the strong family history of malignant melanoma?
questions.explanation:
Hereditary or familial melanoma is currently estimated to account for approximately 10% of all cases of melanoma.
It is defined by families in which at least 2 first-degree relatives (or alternatively at least 3 members with any degree of relationship) have had melanoma.
Germ-line mutation in the CDKN2A gene, a regulator of celldivision, is the most common cause of hereditary melanoma.
The lifetime risk for malignant melanoma In someone carrying a CDKN2A gene mutation is nearly 30%.
Other heritable mutations that carry an increased risk of malignant melanoma include CDK4, RBl, MDm2TYR, TYRPl, ASIP and MClR genes.
The MClR gene encodes the melanocortin-1 receptor. This promotes eumelanin production, thereby controlling the ratio of eumelanin and pheomelanin. Polymorphisms that reduce the ability of the melanocortin-1 receptor result in melanocytes making mostly pheomelanin. These are associated with red hair, fair skin and freckles. Whilst such polymorphisms are associated with increased risk of melanoma and non-melanoma skin cancers, the relative risk is much smaller.
Non-inherited or somatic gane mutations that increase the risk of melanoma include those in NRAS, B-RAF and C-KIT. Interestingly, NRAS mutations are more frequent in mucosal melanomas in the head and neck region, in comparison to 8-RAF and C-KIT.

questions.stem: A 31-year-old woman has BRAF-positive stage 4 malignant melanomc1. Which of the following treatments offers her the best prognosis?
questions.explanation:
Vemurafenib is a small molecule inhibitor of the B-RAF enzyme.
Delivery is via the oral route.
ipilumumab would be first line for BRAF-negative disease.

questions.stem: A 53-year man has BRAF-negative stage 4 malignant melanoma. Which of the following treatments would afford him the best prognosis?
questions.explanation:
ipilimumab is monoclonI antibody that up-regulates immune-surveillanceby targeting CTLA-4 (an inhibitory protein on cytotoxic T cells)
Delivery is via the intravenous route
Vemurafenib would not be indicated for BRAF-negative disease

questions.stem: A 31-year-old woman is to start ipilimumab for BRAf-negative stage 4 malignant melanoma. What is the most common complicating autoimmune reaction seen with this monoclonal antibody?
questions.explanation:
CTLA-4 inhibition can trigger numerous autoi-mmune phenomena
The most common of these is autoimmune colitis, manifesting with such symptoms as abdominal pain and bloody diarrhoea

questions.stem: A patient with stage 4 melanoma presents with her second squamous cell carcinoma since starting a new medication. Which of the following therapies is she most likely to be receiving?
questions.explanation:
Dabrafenib and Vemurafenib are B-RAF enzyme inhibitors.
Their most common side effects concern photosensitivity, other skin eruptions and flu-like symptoms.
Approximately 25% of patients develop skin cancers, espe::ially squamous cell carcinoma.

questions.stem: A 40-year-old woman presented with longstanding translucent yellow, small papules appearing predominantly on her peri-orbital skin. Clinically, you make the diagnosis of syringomas. Which of the following statements is incorrect?
options: Carbon dioxide laser can be used for treating thiscondition.
Electron microscopy studies have identified deposits of calcium.
The eruptive forms can be associated with Ehlers-Danlos syndrome.
These lesions arise from the intradermal portions of the eccrine sweat ducts.
These lesions arise from the outer hair root sheath.
questions.explanation:
Tricholemmomal cysts arise from the outer hair root sheath.
Typically, the histology is of dermal tumours comprising of smali ducts of cuboidal cells with moderately eosinophilic cytoplasmic cords set in a fibrous s·troma creating a comma-shaped appearance.
The eruptive forms of syringomas have also been linked with Marfan's and Down's syndromes.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements regarding dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans is correct?
options: Chromosomal abnormality, which can be present in this condition, is EWS- Fll1.
Erlotinib can be used in some cases.
Metastases are extremely common in this condition.
Positive CD34 with negative Factor XIIIa.
This condition is characterised immunohistochemically by CD34 negative and Factor XIIIa positive.
questions.explanation:
Dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans is a spindle cell tumour with its main differential being dermatofibroma.
Dermatofibromas are classically Factor XIIIa positive and CD34 negative (the reverse is true for dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans).
Chromosomal abnormalities may occur due to translocation of chromosomes 17 and 22, leading to over-ei-pression of platelet-derived growth factor receptor and treatment with imatinib, (particularly if unresectable, recurrent and metastatic), can be used in this condition.
Erlotinib is an epidermal growth factor receptor antagonist and can be used in certain cases of solid tumours.
Dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans can metastasise in about 10 - 15% of cases and surgical excision is the first line treatment of choice (Mohs mlcrographic surgery when available).

questions.stem: A 57-year-old Caucasian woman presented with anine month history of a5 x 5 cm solitary erythematous plaque with overlying telangiectasia on her right shoulder. She did not have any associated pruritus or lymphadenopathy. An incisional biopsy from the plaque showed diffuse dermal subcutaneous lymphocytic infiltrate that spared the epidermis and the cells were positive for CD20, bcl-2 and negative for CD3, CDS, CD10 and bcl-6. The most likely diagnosis here is:
options: Primary cutaneous B-cell lymphoma of diffuse large cell lymphoma type.
Primary cutaneous B-cell lymphoma of marginal zone type.
Primary cutaneous B-cell lymphoma of the follicle centre type.
questions.explanation:
Cutaneous lymphomas are divided into T and B-cell lymphomas.
B-cell lymphomas are sub-divided into diffuse large cell B-lymphoma leg type, marginal B-cell lymphoma and follicle centre.
Marginal zone lymphomas are characterised by positivity to bcl-2 and negativity for bcl-6.
Follicle centre B-cell lymphomas are characterised by positivity to bcl-6 with negativity to bcl-2.
CD20 and CD79a are both markers of B-cells.
B-cell lymphomas, unlike T-cefl lymphomas, do not exhibit epiderrnotroplsm except in rare occasions.
Mycosis fungoides is the commonest type of cutaneous T cell lymphoma.

questions.stem: Which of the following drugs may result in resolution of actinic keratoses?
questions.explanation:
Capecitabine is a chemotherapy agent, which is used in the treatment of certain solid tumours.
Capecitabine is a pro-drug of 5-Fluorouracil (5-FU), which is well known to be effective in the treatment of actinic keratosis in its topical form efudlx cream.
Hydroxyurea has been reported to induce squamous cell carcinomas in some cases.

questions.stem: A 54-year-old man presents with a squamous cell carcinoma. Which of the following is not a risk factor for non-melanoma skin cancers?
questions.explanation:
The risk of development of non-melanoma skin cancer depends on genotypic, phenotypic, and environmental factors.
The risk is the greatest in residents of high ambient solar irradiance who have markers of ultraviolet (UV) susceptibility, such as light skin, eye, and hair colour, or an inability to tan, and those with benign sun-related skin disorders-e.g., actinic keratoses and solar lentigines.
The following are risk factors for non melanoma skin cancers: Solar UV radiation, human papillomavirus, iatrogenic immunosuppression, HIV/AIDS and non-Hodgkin lymphoma, PUVA therapy, photosensitising drugs, UVB radiation, ionising radiation, occupational factors, arsenic and tobacco smoking.

questions.stem: A 35-year-old patient with naevoid basal-cell carcinoma svndrome presents with a cluster of basal cell carcinomas on the back. Which of the following treatments is contra-indicated in the treatment of these basal cell carcinomas?
questions.explanation: Patients withnaevoid basal-cell carcinoma syndrome have increased sensitivity to radiation and a tendency to develop several basal-cell carcinomas in the irradiated field; radiotherapy is therefore contra-indicated in these patients.

questions.stem: A 40-year-old man has had two sebaceous carcinomas excised within the last 5 years and reports that both his father and sister have had several sebaceous carcinomas and sebaceous adenomas excised. The most common malignancy associated with this disorder is:
questions.explanation:
Muir-Torre syndrome is an autosomal dominant syndrome where patients develop sebaceous adenomas or carcinomas and this is associated with internil malignancies with colorectal cancers accounting for nearly half of all the tumours.
Genito-urinary, breast and lung cancers can also occur with this disease.
Sebaceous hyperplasia is not associated with Muir-Torre syndrome.

questions.stem: A 60-year-old man who is on warfarin for metallic aortic valve replacement presents with a 1.5cm nodular basal cell carcinoma on the dorsal aspect of his hand. He is very reluctant to have this treated surgically and wishes for alternative treatment. You discuss the option of radiotherapy and have decided to refer him to the radiotherapist. Which mode of radiotherapy is used for the treatment of basal cell carcinoma7
questions.explanation:
Radiotherapy can be used for basal cell and squamous cell carcinomas if there are contra-indications for surgery.
Superficial x-ray is the treatment of choice in basal cell carcinoma with the use of high dose radical radiation.
Brachytherapy is a method used where an implant is placed followed by high dose radiation. This is often used for Kaposi's sarcoma.
Photodynamic therapy can be used for superficial basal cell carcinomas but not those 0f the nodular type.

questions.stem: A patient presents with nail pigmentation. There is no history of trauma. Which of the following features in a nail would make the diagnosis of acral melanoma more likely than longitudinal melanonychia?
questions.explanation:
Digital or acral melanoma can be tricky to diagnose and any suspicious pigmented streak in a nail should be biopsied to exclude this diagnosis.
Longitudinal melanonychia is its main differential and often presents with multiple digital involvement, skin type V/VI, narrow bands with clear margins, uniform colour, and presence since childhood or puberty.
Accompanying nail dystrophy is not a feature in benign melanonychia and should alert the dermatologist to the possible diagnosis of melanoma.

questions.stem: A 37-year-old man with background of HIV infection presented with a 3-month history of asymptomatic purple-coloured plaques on the lower legs which have failed to respond to topical therapy given by his GP. Biopsy showed a vascular lesion and further immunostaining confirmed the endothelial nature of the lesion. Which of the following is implicated in the pathogenesis of this disease?
questions.explanation:
The diagnosis here is Kaposi's sarcoma which is an angioproliferative tumour arising from endothelial cells.
Human Herpes Virus (HHV) 8 is Implicated in the pathogenesis.
Kaposi's sarcoma has 4 forms: classic, endemic (African), iatrogenic (secondary to immunosuppressive therapy) and AIDS-related.
HHV 8 is also implicated in the pathogenesis of Castleman's disease.
HHV 2 is HSV-2 subtype, HHV 4 is Epstein-Barr virus, and HHV 6 is implicated in the pathogenesis of roseola infantum.

questions.stem: A 76-vear old man presnnted with a 6-month history of a slowly growing plaque on the forehead. Examination showed a purplil;h plaque mimicking a bruise with some vascular-looking papules. A biopsy showed a tumour arising from the vascular bed with marked atypia and mitoses. The most likely diagnosis is:
questions.explanation:
Angiosarcoma is an aggressive vascular tumour with high recurrence rate and potential for metastasis to the lung, liver and brain.
The 3 clinical settings of angiosarcoma are: (i) in the elderly (predominantly head and neck), (ii) at sites of lymphoedema, and (iii) radiotherapy-related.
Kaposi's sarcoma is in the differential but there is no atypia and the tumour arises from both the endothelial and spindle cells and unlike angiosarcoma, shows positivity for HHV 8.

questions.stem: A patient with a metallic mitral valve attends the dermatological surge,-y department for an excision of a small nodular basal cell carcinoma on his chest. What should be the most appropriate action with regards to antibiotic prophylaxis for his metallic valve?
options: A one-week course of penicillin after the procedure.
Penicillin and metronidazole single doses should be given.
Single penicillin dose one hour prior to the procedure.
questions.explanation:
The current consensus is that dermatological surgical procedures confer a low risk for endocarditis, and therefore, no prophylactic antibiotics are required.
An assessment should however, still take place based on individual circumstances.

questions.stem: A 30-year-old patient with polycystic ovarian syndrome was referred for laser treatment of facial hirsutism. The following hair-skin combination is considered best for laser treatment:
questions.explanation:
Skin phototype 2 - dark terminal hair is considered the best combination for successful laser hair removal with the currently available lasers and light devices including intense pulsed light, long pulsed Nd:YAG, diode and Alexandrite lasers.
This combination results in best clinical outcomes with least side effects.
Skin phototype 1 patients rarely have dark terminal hairs.

questions.stem: A 30-year-old patient with polycystic ovarian syndrome was referred for laser treatment of facial hirsutism. She is currently using topical eflornithine cream. Your advice, based on current recommendation is:
options: Continue treatment with eflornithine cream, but stop for few days after laser treatment.
Stop eflornithine cream for 3 months prior to laser treatment.
Stop eflornithine cream for 6 months prior to laser treatment.
Stop eflornithine cream for 12 months prior to laser treatment.
questions.explanation: Av.:1ilable evidence suggests that addition of eflornithine to laser treatment results in a more rapid and complete reduction of unwanted facial hair in women when the combination is used for up to 6 months.

questions.stem: A 45-year-old woman wants treatment of her tattoo. Which laser would be the most appropriate for the treatment of her red professional tattoo?
questions.explanation: QS Nd:YAG (532 nm) emits green light and is the treatment of chioce for red tattoos.

questions.stem: A 25-year-old woman has facial pigmentation, which has been formally diagnosed as melasma. Which of the following is the recommended laser treatment for melasma?
questions.explanation: Treatment of melasma with pigment specific lasers is disappointing and as such i.s not recommended.

questions.stem: Which of the following types of botulinum toxin is most commonly used in the treatment of hyperkinetic facial lines?
questions.explanation: Tliere are seven distinct serotypes of botulinum toxin: A, B, Cl, D, E, F and G.

questions.stem: A 40-year-old woman attends for botulinum toxin injection to treat glabellar lines. Which of the following concurrent treatment would not be considered a contra-indication for botulinum toxin injection?
questions.explanation: The listed drugs can potentiate the action of botox, which should be avoided if the patient is on any of these medications.

questions.stem: A GO-year old patient is interested in treatment of his deep glabellar lines. Which of the following is considered the safest in the treatment of deep glabellar lines?
questions.explanation:
Local skin necrosis has been reported following deep glabellar injection of bovine collagen induced vascular occlusion.
Loss of vision due to arterial embolization has been reported with both bovine collagen and alltologous fat injected into the glabellar region.

questions.stem: Which of the following chemical peels is associated with a risk of cardiac toxicity?
questions.explanation: Cardiac arrhythmias and laryngeal oedema have been reported with phenoi peels. Precautions recommended at the time of phenol peels inc.lude appropriate analgesia, adequate hydration, and availability of cardiac monitoring and resusc.itation Equipment.

questions.stem: A 56-year-old, normally fit and well, man presented with a 2 cmtelangiectatic pearly lesion on the forehead but with rather indistinctive scar-like margin. What would be the most appropriate therapeutic intervention?
options: Simple excision with a 4 mm margin.
questions.explanation:
This is a morphoeic basal cell carcinoma and therefore Mohs' micrographit surgery is the most appropriate intervention.
Other indications for this type of surgery include recurrent basal cell carcinomas, large tumours (size > 2 cm), aggressive histology (metaplastic, infiltrative, morphoeic and micro-nodular) and high-risk sites (forehead and around the eyes, nose and ears).

questions.stem: A 3-year-old girl is referred to paediatric dermatology with a vascular malformation on the left side of the face. She is under the care of the neurologists for epilepsy. The condition is diagnosed as Sturge-Weber syndrome. Which of the following lasers will be most appropriate for treating this vascular deformity?
questions.explanation:
Pulsed dye laser (PDL) was the first vascular specific laser used for the treatment of port-wine stains.
It is still the gold standard for the treatment of port-wine stains.
The chromophore for 585 nm and 595 nm wavelengths (PDL) is haemoglobin.
The selective heating of haemoglobin by these wavelengths results in destructlcn of the aberrant vessels.
Deeper vascular malformations may respond to the Nd:YAG laser.

questions.stem: A 70-year-old woman presents with bluish-grey pigmentation on the forehead. She had been on long-term minocycline for bullous pemphigoid She is seeking your advice on laser treatment. Which of the following lasers is likely to be effective in the treatment of her forehead pigmentation?
questions.explanation:
Minocycline pigmentation would resolve without active intervention and adequate sun protection.
The Q-switched lasers (Nd:YAG, Alexandrite and Ruby)111 be effective in lightening the pigmentation.

questions.stem: In which of the following conditions would you institute prophylactic antibiotics prior to dermatological surgery procedures on a contaminated wound?
questions.explanation:
Antibiotic prophylaxis for dermatologic surgery is indicated for:
High risk cardiac conditions:
Prosthetic cardiac valve or prosthetic material used for valve repair.
Prior infective endocarditis.
Cardiac transplant recipients who develop valvulopathy.
Congenital heart disease.
High risk prosthetic joint indications:
First 2 years post joint replacement.
immunosuppressed patients.
Malnourishment, malignancy, haemophilia, type 1 diabetes.
Prophylaxis is not indicated for simple biopsies, curettage or excision. It is, however, indicated for procedures, especially Mohs' surgery, ar,d when reconstruction lasts >20 minutes and when the wound is contaminated or infected.

questions.explanation:
Beside the above the following tips help to decrease pain with local anaesthetic injections:
Topical anaesthetic.
Buffer with sodium bicarbonate.
l'lject slowly through a dilated pore or wound edge.
Deeper injections into subcutaneous area.
Minimal needle punctures.
Consider ringblocks.

questions.stem: Which of the following is not an amide anaesthetic?
questions.explanation:
Procaine, chloroprocaine and tetracaine are Ester anaesthetics.
Lignocaine, mepivacaine, prilocaine and bupivacaine are Amide anaesthetics.
Amide anaesthetics are more commonly used in skin surgery and can easily be remembered as they contain the letter "I".

questions.stem: A 35-year-old woman presents with ptosis of her left upper eyelid 4 days following botulinum toxin injections for forehead wrinkles. What is the best treatment?
questions.explanation: Apraclonidine eye drops (alpha 2 adrenergic agonist) are used to reverse the ptosis induced by botulinum toxin injections.

questions.stem: Which of the following nerves is not a branch of the trigeminal nerve?
questions.explanation:
Marginal mandibular is a branch of the facial nerve, which is a motor nerve.
The trigeminal nerve is a sensory nerve.
All the above branches of the trigeminal nerve supply the eyelids and skin around the eyes.

questions.stem: The sensory innervation of the vertex of the scalp is predominantly by which nerve?
questions.explanation:
Th supra-trochlear nerve innervates part of the frontal scalp.
The auriculotemporal nerve innervates the parietal part and the lesser occipital parieto-occipital part of the scalp behind the ear. PQ.2

questions.stem: Which of the following nerves is not a branch of the ophthalmic division of trigeminal (Vl.) nerve?
questions.explanation:
The infra-orbital nerve is a branch of the maxillary branch (V2) of the trigeminal nerve.
Other branches of the maxillary branch (V2) include the zygomaticofaclal and zvgomaticotemporal nerves.
The external nasal nerve 1s a branch of the ophthalmic division of trigeminal (Vl) nerve.

questions.stem: You remove a tumour from the right nasal ala and decide to reconstruct the defect with a full thickness skin graft. One of the following factors does not reduce the survival of the graft:
options: Cartilage at the base of the defect.
The presence of a fat layer at the base of the graft.
questions.explanation:
Full thickness skin graft can be used as a method of reconstruction for certain defects particularly on the nasal alae, ears, lower eyelids and temple.
Several factors cari influence the survival Clf the graft tissue and it is important to be aware of these.
Donor sites skin should match the skin colour and texture of the recipient site and are is often harvested from the pre-or post-auricular or sites or from the supra-clavicular area.

questions.stem: A tumour was removed from theconchal bowl. This defect measures 10x8 mm and is fairly superficial with intact periosteum. Which of the following reconstructive options is the most suitable in thiscase:
questions.explanation:
Secondary intention healing can be a suitable option particularly in the conchal bowl, medial canthus, scalp, forehead and the dorsum of the hands and feet.
As the wound heals a degree of contraction will occur and it is essential to monitor that the contraction force does not result in an unwanted pull on a free margin such as the eyebrow or nasal ala.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an ablative laser?
questions.explanation:
Ablation is simply the removal of tissue and in the cases of laser ablation is due to vaporization of the tissue.
Other ablative laser modality is carbon dioxide laser.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the most commonly observed side effect of pulsed dye laser treatment?
questions.explanation:
Bruising may last up to 2 weeks if a purpuric mode has been used.
In some instances, if a non-purpuric mode (often with longer pulse duration and lower fluence) is used, results may take require several more treatments to achieve a similar outcomes as to the purpuric mode.
All other side-effects mentioned in the answers are possible, but are less frequent.

questions.stem: Which of the following isa sensory nerve?
questions.explanation:
All facial sensory nerves are branches of the trigeminal nerve.
The motor nerves of the face are branches of the facial nerve and are the tempo.al, zygomatic, buccal, marginal mandibular, and cervical nerves.
In facial skin surgery the Z danger zones t:1at every dermatologist should be ciware of are the anatomic location of both the temporal and marginal mandibuiar nerves.

questions.stem: How does the novel oral anticoagulant dabigatran work?
options: Inhibition of activated vitamin K synthesis.
questions.explanation:
Unlike warfarin, novel oral anticoagulants act independently of the vitamin K pathway and, because of shorter half-lives and more predictable pharmacokinetics, do not require routine therapeutic monitoring
Answer B is true for the novel oral anticoagulants rivaroxiban and apixaban
Answer A is true for warfarin
Answer D is true for heparin

questions.stem: Which of the following absorbable and non-absorbable suture combinations will minimise the suture reaction and scarring·?
questions.explanation:
PDS (polydioxanone) eliclt3 the greatest scar reaction amongst the absorbable sutures listed and Monocryl the least.
Ethllon elicits a greater scar reaction than Prolene.
The extent of the scar reaction can also be reduced by using a smaller calibre suture anC: avoiding delayed suture removal.

questions.stem: What is the protein target of local anaesthetics?
questions.explanation:
Local anaesthetics comprise a lipophilic aromatic region attached to a basic amine side chain. For aminoesters this is via an ester link and for aminoamides this is via amide link.
Local anaesthetics block propagation of action potentials of sensory neurons by use-dependent inhibition of voltage-gated Na receptors, binding to a site within the open pore.

questions.stem: Following surgery for excision of a basal cell carcinoma, an 85-year-old patient presents with asymmetrical smile. Injury to the following nerve is most likely:
questions.explanation:
The marginal mandibular nerve lies along the body of the mandible-(80%) or within 1-2 cm below (20%). Although it lies deep to the platysma throughout much of its course it becomes more superficial approximately 2 cm lateral to the corner of the mouth and ends on the under surface of the muscles.
Injury to the marginal mandibular nerve results in paralysis of the depressors of the corner of the mouth.

questions.stem: A 35-year-old woman has residual telangiectasiae and erythema following i;uccessful treatment of the papulo-pustular element of rosacea wi h iymecycline. She is keen for treatment of her facial telangiectasiae and erythema. Which of the following is the best treatment?
questions.explanation: Pulsed dye laser at 595nm is the treatment of choice for most vascular lesions. An other laser that is commonly used for the treatment of telangiectasiae is the KTP laser (frequency doubled, Nd:YAG laser).

questions.stem: A 55-year-old lady is undergoing excision of an atypical naevus on her shoulder. You are about to inject 2%llgnocaine with adrenaline. Contra-indication for this anaesthetic would include?
questions.explanation:
Anaesthetic solutions containing adrenaline should not be used if patients are taking non-selective beta-blockers, such as propranolol.
In these situations plain lignocaine should be used instead.
A risk of developing a hypotensive crisis is small, nevertheless it is considered good and safe practice to enquire about medications; in particular, for propranolol.

questions.stem: Q-Switched <1lexandrite laser is reported to be useful for removal of green tattoos. The wave length of Q-Switched alexandrite laser is:
questions.explanation:
Q-Switched Ruby laser has a wave length of 694 nm whilst Erbium YAG has a wave length of 2940 nm.
CO2 laser has a wavelength the far infrared region of 10600 nm.

questions.stem: The maximum adult dose for plain lignocaine as a local anaesthetic is:
questions.explanation:
Lignocaine is widely used as a local anaesthetic In dermatology and the maximum safe volumes need to be known.
For plain lignocaine, the maximum safe adult does is 3mg/kg, however this is 7mg/kg when mixed with adrenaline. This is based on 1% lignocaine concentration.
Symptoms of lignocainE:toxicity include drowsiness, tingling, numbness of the lips, tinnitus and a metallic taste.
In severe toxicity, convulsions and respiratory arrest can occur.
1 ml of 1% lignocaine contains 10 mg of lignocaine.

questions.stem: The least painful local anaesthetic is:
questions.explanation:
o.s% plain lignocaine is the least painful of the local anaesthetics; however, its action may be too short for complicated procedures.
1% lignocaine combined with adrenaline has a longer action; larger amounts are required for reaching the maximum safe volume compared to 2% lignocaine with adrenaline.
Bupivacaine has a prolonged duration of action and is therefore used for long procedures and post-operative analgesia.

questions.stem: A 63-year-old man presented with a nc,dular oasal cell carcinoma on the left side: of his forehead above his eyebrow which was excised. Two weeks following the excision, he is still complaining of the inability to raise his left eyebrow which results in a droopy left eyebrow. Which nerve has been damaged during the procedure?
options: Marginal mandibular branch of facial nerve.
questions.explanation:
The temporal branch of the facial nerve innervates the frontalis and the upper portion of the orbicularis oculi.
Damage to the marginal mandibular branch of the facial nerve will result in drooping of the mouth and the inability to evert the lip laterally and inferiorly.
Damage to the great auricular nerve will result in numbness of the inferior two thirds of the ear and the adjacent cheek and neck area.
Damage to the spinal accessory nerve will result in a winged scapula (the inability to shrug the shoulder and abduct the arm).
